title.zh: 卷五十七 列傳第四十五: 周宗室
title.en: Volume 57 Biographies 45: The Northern Zhou Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷五十七 列傳第四十五: 周宗室 Volume 57 Biographies 45: The Northern Zhou Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 邵惠公顥子什肥導護叱羅協馮遷杞簡公連莒莊公洛生虞國公仲廣川公測弟深深子孝伯東平公神舉弟慶

translations.literal: Duke Hui of Shao Hao; sons Shifen, Dao, and Hu; Chi Luoxie; Feng Qian; Duke Lian of Qi; Duke Luosheng of Ju; Duke Zhong of Yuguo; Duke Ce of Guangchuan, younger brother Shen, Shen's son Xiaobo; Duke Shenju of Dongping, younger brother Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao; his sons Shifen, Yuwen Dao, and Yuwen Hu; Chi Luoxie; Feng Qian; Duke Lian of Qi; Duke Luosheng of Ju; Duke Zhong of Yuguo; Duke Ce of Guangchuan, his younger brother Shen, Shen's son Xiaobo; Duke Shenju of Dongping, and his younger brother Qing.

sentences.zh: 邵惠公顥，周文帝之長兄也。

translations.literal: Duke Hui of Shao Hao was the eldest elder brother of Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao was the eldest elder brother of Zhou Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 德皇帝娶樂浪王氏，是為德皇后。

translations.literal: The De Emperor married the Wang clan of Lelang; she became Empress De.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor De Yuwen Gong married Lady Wang of Lelang; she became Empress De.

sentences.zh: 生顥，性至孝，居德皇后喪，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: She bore Hao; his nature was supremely filial; during Empress De's mourning he grieved beyond ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Yuwen Hao, who was supremely filial; while mourning Empress De, his grief went beyond what ritual allowed.

sentences.zh: 德皇帝與衛可瑰戰，墜馬，顥與數騎奔救，乃免。

translations.literal: When the De Emperor fought Wei Keugui, he fell from his horse; Hao with several horsemen rushed to rescue him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor De fought Wei Keugui and fell from his horse, Yuwen Hao galloped to his aid with a few riders and enabled him to escape.

sentences.zh: 顥遂戰歿。

translations.literal: Hao then died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hao then fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大塚宰，封邵國公，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was posthumously granted grand chancellor, enfeoffed as Duke of Shao state, posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), Yuwen Hao was posthumously granted grand chancellor, enfeoffed as Duke of Shao, and given the posthumous title Hui (Benevolent).

sentences.zh: 三子，什肥、導、護。

translations.literal: Three sons: Shifen, Dao, and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Shifen, Yuwen Dao, and Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 什肥事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shifen served his mother; his filial piety was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen served his mother with a filial devotion that became renowned.

sentences.zh: 文帝入關，不能離母，遂留晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen entered Guan, he could not leave his mother and therefore remained at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai entered Guan, Shifen could not leave his mother and remained at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 文帝定秦、隴，什肥為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Duke of Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Tai had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Gao Huan, Duke of Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小塚宰，襲爵邵國公，諡曰景。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was posthumously granted grand general and junior grand chancellor, inherited the title Duke of Shao state, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), Shifen was posthumously granted grand general and junior grand chancellor, succeeded to the title Duke of Shao, and was given the posthumous title Jing (Resplendent).

sentences.zh: 子胄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuwen Zhou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 胄少孤，頗有幹略。

translations.literal: Zhou was orphaned young and had considerable initiative and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou was orphaned young and showed considerable drive and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 景公之見害，以年幼下蠶室。

translations.literal: When Duke Jing was killed, because of his young age he was sent to the castration quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Jing was killed, Yuwen Zhou, because of his youth, was sent to the castration quarters.

sentences.zh: 保定初，詔以晉公護子會紹景公封。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, an edict ordered that Duke of Jin Hu's son Hui should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), an edict ordered that Yuwen Hui, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 天和中，與齊通好，胄歸，襲爵邵國公。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era, when peace with Qi was established, Zhou returned and inherited the title Duke of Shao state.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era (566–572), when peace was made with Northern Qi, Yuwen Zhou returned and inherited the title Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝輔政，胄為滎州刺史，舉兵應尉遲迥，為清河公楊素所殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Zhou was governor of Xing Province; he raised troops to support Yuchi Jiong and was killed by Prince of Qinghe Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian served as regent, Yuwen Zhou was governor of Xing Province; he raised troops to support Yuchi Jiong and was killed by Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 國除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ducal fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 會字乾仁，胄至自齊，改封譚國公。

translations.literal: Hui, style name Ganren; when Zhou returned from Qi, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tan state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hui, style name Ganren; when Yuwen Zhou returned from Northern Qi, Hui's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 後與護同誅。

translations.literal: Later he was executed together with Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed together with Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，追復封爵常武公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, his enfeoffment was posthumously restored as Duke of Changwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), his title was posthumously restored as Duke of Changwu.

sentences.zh: 導字菩薩，少雄豪。

translations.literal: Dao, style name Pusa; in youth he was bold and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dao, style name Pusa, was bold and heroic in youth.

sentences.zh: 初與諸父在葛榮中，榮敗，遷晉陽。

translations.literal: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's forces; when Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's army; when Ge Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 與文帝隨賀拔岳入關，常從征伐。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen with Helba Yue into Guan and constantly joined campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuwen Tai with Helba Yue into Guan and constantly joined the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 文帝討侯莫陳悅，導追斬之牽屯山，以功封饒陽縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Houmochen Yue, Dao pursued and beheaded him at Qiantun Mountain; for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Raoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai campaigned against Houmochen Yue, Yuwen Dao pursued and beheaded him at Qiantun Mountain; for this merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Raoyang county.

sentences.zh: 及魏文帝東征，留導為華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Yuwen Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 既而趙青雀、於伏德、慕容思慶等作亂，導禽伏德，斬思慶，屯渭橋會文帝軍。

translations.literal: Soon Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled; Dao captured Fude, beheaded Siqing, camped at Wei Bridge, and joined Emperor Wen's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled, Yuwen Dao captured Yu Fude, beheaded Murong Siqing, camped at Wei Bridge, and joined Yuwen Tai's army.

sentences.zh: 及事平，進爵章武郡公，加侍中。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery and given palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery and appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密以北豫州降，文帝東征，復以導為大都督，行華州刺史，甚得守扞之方。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu, Emperor Wen marched east; Dao was again made grand commander and acting governor of Hua Province, and was very skilled in methods of defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu and Yuwen Tai marched east, Yuwen Dao was again made grand commander and acting governor of Hua Province, and mastered methods of defense.

sentences.zh: 及大軍不利，東魏追至稠桑，知關中有備，乃退。

translations.literal: When the main army suffered a setback, Eastern Wei pursued as far as Chousang; learning Guanzhong was prepared, they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army suffered a setback, Eastern Wei pursued to Chousang; finding Guanzhong ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侯景來附，詔征隴右大都督獨孤信東下，令導代信為秦州刺史、大都督、十五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came to submit, an edict summoned Longyou grand commander Dugu Xin east; Dao was ordered to replace Xin as governor of Qin Province, grand commander, and commander of military affairs in fifteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing came over, an edict summoned Longyou grand commander Dugu Xin east; Yuwen Dao was ordered to replace him as governor of Qin Province, grand commander, and commander of military affairs in fifteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 及齊氏稱帝，文帝討之，魏文帝遣齊王廓鎮隴右，征導拜大將軍、大都督、二十三州諸軍事，屯咸陽。

translations.literal: When the Qi house declared itself emperor, Emperor Wen campaigned against it; Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Kuo to guard Longyou, summoned Dao, and appointed him grand general, grand commander, and commander of military affairs in twenty-three provinces, stationing him at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi declared itself emperor, Yuwen Tai campaigned against it; Western Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Yuwen Kuo to guard Longyou, summoned Yuwen Dao, and appointed him grand general, grand commander, and commander of military affairs in twenty-three provinces, stationing him at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 大軍還，乃旋舊鎮。

translations.literal: When the main army returned, he then returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 導性寬明，善撫禦，文帝每出征，導恆居守，深為吏人所附，朝廷重之。

translations.literal: Dao's nature was magnanimous and clear-sighted; he was skilled at governing and controlling; whenever Emperor Wen campaigned, Dao always remained to guard; officials and commoners were deeply attached to him, and the court valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dao was magnanimous and clear-sighted and skilled at governing; whenever Yuwen Tai campaigned, Dao stayed behind to guard the rear; officials and commoners were deeply attached to him, and the court valued him.

sentences.zh: 薨于上邽，魏帝遣侍中、漁陽王綱監護喪事，贈尚書令，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: He died at Shanggui; the Wei emperor sent palace attendant Prince of Yuyang Gang to oversee the funeral, granted him Minister over the Masses posthumously, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Shanggui; the Wei emperor sent palace attendant Prince of Yuyang Yuwen Gang to oversee the funeral, granted him Minister over the Masses posthumously, and gave him the posthumous title Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 朝議以導撫和西戎，威恩顯著，欲令世鎮隴右，以彰厥德。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that because Dao had pacified the western Rong and his authority and kindness were prominent, they wished to have his line hereditarily command Longyou to manifest his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that because Yuwen Dao had pacified the western Rong and his authority and kindness were conspicuous, they wished his line to command Longyou for generations to manifest his virtue.

sentences.zh: 乃葬上邽城西無疆原，華戎會葬者萬餘人，奠祭于路，悲號振野，皆曰「我君舍我乎」。

translations.literal: He was buried on Wujiang plain west of Shanggui city; Chinese and foreigners attending the funeral numbered more than ten thousand; offerings were made along the road; wailing shook the wilds; all said, "Has our lord abandoned us?"
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Wujiang plain west of Shanggui; more than ten thousand Chinese and frontier peoples attended the funeral; offerings lined the road and wailing shook the countryside; all cried, "Has our lord abandoned us?"

sentences.zh: 大小相與負土成墳，高五十餘尺，周回八十餘步。

translations.literal: Young and old together carried earth to form a tumulus, more than fifty chi high and more than eighty bu in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old together carried earth to build a mound more than fifty chi high and more than eighty paces around.

sentences.zh: 為官司所止，然後泣辭而去。

translations.literal: Officials stopped them; only then did they weep and take their leave.
translations.idiomatic: Government officers stopped them; only then did the mourners weep and depart.

sentences.zh: 天和五年，重贈太師、柱國、豳國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe, he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state, and Duke of Bin state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhe (568), he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state, and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 導五子，廣、亮、翼、椿、眾。

translations.literal: Dao had five sons: Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dao had five sons: Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 亮、椿出後於杞。

translations.literal: Liang and Chun were given in adoption to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Chun were given in adoption to the Qi line.

sentences.zh: 廣字乾歸，少方嚴，好文學。

translations.literal: Guang, style name Qiangui; in youth he was stern and proper and loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Guang, style name Qiangui, was stern and proper in youth and loved literature.

sentences.zh: 武成初，位大將軍、梁州總管，進封蔡國公，累遷秦州刺史、總管十三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the early Wucheng era, he held the post of grand general and area commander of Liang Province, was advanced to Duke of Cai state, and was repeatedly transferred to governor of Qin Province and area commander of military affairs in thirteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was grand general and area commander of Liang Province, was advanced to Duke of Cai, and later became governor of Qin Province and area commander of military affairs in thirteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 性明察，善撫綏，人庶畏悅之。

translations.literal: His nature was clear-sighted; he was skilled at comforting and governing; the people revered and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: He was clear-sighted and skilled at comforting and governing; the people revered him and were pleased with his rule.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護諸子及廣弟杞公亮等侈靡逾制，廣獨率禮，又折節待士，朝野稱焉。

translations.literal: At the time the sons of Duke of Jin Hu and Guang's younger brother Duke of Qi Liang and others were extravagant beyond regulations; Guang alone followed ritual; he also lowered himself to treat scholars; court and countryside praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the sons of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu and Guang's younger brother Duke of Qi Yuwen Liang and others lived beyond their rank; Guang alone kept to ritual, humbled himself to treat scholars, and won praise in court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 曾侍于武帝所，食瓜美，持以奉進，帝悅之。

translations.literal: Once while attending at Emperor Wu's place, he found the melon delicious, held it to present it, and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong, he found the melon delicious, presented it to the emperor, and pleased him.

sentences.zh: 廣以晉公護擅權，勸令挹損，護不能納。

translations.literal: Guang, because Duke of Jin Hu monopolized power, urged him to restrain himself; Hu could not accept the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu monopolized power, Guang urged him to restrain himself; Hu would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 後除陝州總管，以病免。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed area commander of Shaan Province and was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed area commander of Shaan Province but was dismissed because of illness.

sentences.zh: 及孝公追封豳國公，召廣襲爵。

translations.literal: When Duke Xiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin state, Guang was summoned to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin, Yuwen Guang was summoned to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 初、廣母李氏以廣患，憂而成疾，遂歿。

translations.literal: At first Guang's mother Lady Li, because of Guang's illness, worried herself into sickness and then died.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yuwen Guang's mother Lady Li, because Guang's illness had worn on, worried herself into sickness and died.

sentences.zh: 廣居喪加篤，乃以毀薨。

translations.literal: Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.

sentences.zh: 世稱母為廣病，廣為母死，慈孝之道，極於一門。

translations.literal: The age said the mother died of Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial piety and kindness reached their utmost in one clan.
translations.idiomatic: People said the mother died of Yuwen Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial devotion in that household reached its utmost.

sentences.zh: 武帝素服親臨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu in plain white mourning garb personally attended.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong in plain white mourning garb personally attended.

sentences.zh: 其故吏儀同李克信等上表褒述，申其宿志，庶存儉約。

translations.literal: His former subordinates commissioner-equal Li Kexin and others submitted a memorial praising and recounting him, stating his longstanding wish, hoping to preserve frugality.
translations.idiomatic: His former subordinates commissioner-equal Li Kexin and others submitted a memorial praising him and stating his longstanding wish that his funeral remain frugal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔河間才藻，追敘于中尉；

translations.literal: The edict said: "Formerly Hejian's literary talent was commemorated by the Commandant of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "In the past, Hejian's literary gifts were praised by the Commandant of Justice;

sentences.zh: 東海謙約，見稱於身後。

translations.literal: Donghai was modest and restrained, and was praised after death.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai's modest restraint was praised after his death.

sentences.zh: 可斟酌前典，率由舊章，使易簀之言，得申遺志，黜殯之請，無虧令終。」

translations.literal: Former canons may be consulted and old regulations followed, so that words of changing the mat may fulfill his dying wish and the request to reduce lavish burial may not mar his fine end."
translations.idiomatic: Let former canons be consulted and old regulations followed, so that his wish to change the mat may be honored and his request for a plain burial may not mar a worthy end."

sentences.zh: 於是贈本官，加太保、隴右十四州諸軍事、秦州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted his former office and additionally made Grand Tutor, commander of military affairs in fourteen Longyou provinces, and governor of Qin Province; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted his former offices and additionally made Grand Tutor, commander of military affairs in fourteen Longyou provinces, and governor of Qin Province; his posthumous title was Wen (Cultured).

sentences.zh: 葬于隴右，所司一遵儉約之典。

translations.literal: He was buried in Longyou; the responsible offices all followed regulations of frugal simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Longyou, and every responsible office followed the regulations for a plain funeral.

sentences.zh: 子洽嗣，隋文輔政，被害，國除。

translations.literal: His son Qia succeeded; when Sui Wen served as regent, he was killed and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qia succeeded; when Yang Jian served as regent, Qia was killed and the ducal fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 翼字乾宜，封西陽郡公，早薨，曰昭。

translations.literal: Yi, style name Qianyi; enfeoffed as Duke of Xiyang commandery; died young; posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, style name Qianyi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiyang commandery; he died young and was given the posthumous title Zhao (Luminous).

sentences.zh: 無子，以杞公亮子溫嗣，後坐亮反誅，國除。

translations.literal: Having no son, Wen, son of Duke of Qi Liang, was made heir; later because Liang rebelled he was executed and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so Wen, son of Duke of Qi Yuwen Liang, succeeded; later, because Liang rebelled, Wen was executed and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 眾字乾道，少不慧，封天水郡公，為隋文所誅。

translations.literal: Zhong, style name Qiandao; in youth he was not clever; enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui commandery; was executed by Sui Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, style name Qiandao, was not clever in youth; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui commandery and was executed by Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 護字薩保，幼方正有志度，特為德皇帝所愛。

translations.literal: Hu, style name Saba; in youth he was upright and principled with resolve and measure; he was especially loved by Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, style name Saba, was upright and principled in youth; Emperor De Yuwen Gong especially loved him.

sentences.zh: 文帝之入關，以年小不從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen entered Guan, because he was young he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai entered Guan, Hu was still too young to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，始自晉陽至平涼，時年十七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he first came from Jinyang to Pingliang; he was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai (531), he first came from Jinyang to Pingliang; he was seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 文帝諸子並幼，遂委以家務，內外無不嚴肅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's sons were all young; he therefore entrusted household affairs to Hu; inside and outside were without exception solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's sons were all still young; he entrusted household affairs to Hu, and within and without the household all was solemn and orderly.

sentences.zh: 文帝歎之，以為類已。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sighed and thought him similar to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sighed and thought him much like himself.

sentences.zh: 及臨夏州，留護事賀拔嶽。

translations.literal: When he went out to govern Xia Province, he left Hu to serve Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai went out to govern Xia Province, he left Yuwen Hu to serve Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶽被害。

translations.literal: Yue was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue was murdered.

sentences.zh: 文帝至平涼，以護為都督，從破侯莫陳悅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen reached Pingliang, he made Hu commander; Hu followed and defeated Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai reached Pingliang, he made Yuwen Hu commander; Hu followed him and helped defeat Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 後以迎魏帝功，封水池縣伯。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in welcoming the Wei emperor, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shuichi county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for helping welcome the Wei emperor, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shuichi county.

sentences.zh: 從文帝禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，戰河橋，並有功。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, defeating at Shawei, and fighting at Heqiao—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, defeating at Shawei, and fighting at Heqiao—all with merit.

sentences.zh: 芒山之役，為敵人所圍，賴都督侯伏龍恩救，乃免。

translations.literal: In the battle of Mount Mang, he was surrounded by the enemy; relying on commander Hou Fulongen's rescue, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle of Mount Mang, he was surrounded by the enemy; only with the rescue of commander Hou Fulongen did he escape.

sentences.zh: 坐免官，尋復本位。

translations.literal: He was relieved of office for the fault; soon he was restored to his original position.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for the fault but soon restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 大統十三年，進封中山公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Datong, he was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Datong (547), he was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was transferred to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (549), he was transferred to grand general.

sentences.zh: 與於謹征江陵，進兵徑至江陵城下，以待大軍至，圍而克之。

translations.literal: With Yu Jin he campaigned against Jiangling; he advanced directly to beneath the walls of Jiangling city, awaiting the great army's arrival, then besieged and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Jin he campaigned against Jiangling; he advanced directly to the walls of Jiangling, waited for the main army to arrive, then besieged and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 師還，護又討平襄陽蠻帥向天保等萬餘落。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Hu again suppressed and pacified the Xiangyang Man chieftain Xiang Tianbao and others, more than ten thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Yuwen Hu again suppressed and pacified the Xiangyang Man chieftain Xiang Tianbao and more than ten thousand families under him.

sentences.zh: 初行六官，拜司空。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices system was first implemented, he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were first instituted, he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 文帝西巡，至牽屯山遇疾，召護至涇州，見文帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen toured west and reached Qiantun Mountain he fell ill; he summoned Hu to Jing Province to see Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai toured west to Qiantun Mountain he fell ill; he summoned Hu to Jing Province to see him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾形容若此，必不濟。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My appearance is like this; surely I will not recover.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "I look like this; I surely will not recover.

sentences.zh: 諸子幼，天下事以屬汝。」

translations.literal: My sons are young; affairs of the realm are entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: My sons are still young; I entrust the realm's affairs to you."

sentences.zh: 護涕泣奉命。

translations.literal: Hu wept tears and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu wept and accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 行至雲陽，文帝崩，護秘之，至長安乃發喪。

translations.literal: When they reached Yunyang, Emperor Wen died; Hu kept it secret; only when they reached Chang'an did he announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yunyang, Yuwen Tai died; Yuwen Hu kept it secret and announced mourning only after reaching Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時嗣子沖幼，強寇在近，人情不安。

translations.literal: At the time the heir Chong was young; powerful enemies were near; people's hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the heir Yuwen Chong was young; powerful enemies were near; people's hearts were unsettled.

sentences.zh: 護綱紀內外，撫循文武，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: Hu maintained order inside and outside and comforted civil and military officers; the hearts of the multitude were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu maintained order inside and outside and comforted civil and military officers; the hearts of the multitude were then settled.

sentences.zh: 先是，文帝常云「我得胡力」，當時莫曉其指，時人以「護」字當之。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Wen had often said, "I obtain Hu's strength"; at the time no one understood the meaning; people matched it to the character for Hu in his name.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuwen Tai had often said, "I obtain Hu's strength"; at the time no one understood what he meant; people later matched it to the character hu in Yuwen Hu's name.

sentences.zh: 尋拜柱國。

translations.literal: Before long he received appointment as pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed pillar-of-state, one of the highest honors of the realm.

sentences.zh: 文帝山陵畢，護以天命有歸，遣諷魏帝以禪代事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen's tomb rites were completed, Hu, because the Mandate had a destination, sent men to hint to the Wei emperor about abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai's tomb rites were completed, Yuwen Hu, believing the Mandate had found its bearer, sent men to hint to the Wei emperor about abdication and succession.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，拜大司馬，封晉國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed grand marshal, enfeoffed as Duke of Jin state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Yuwen Hu was appointed grand marshal, enfeoffed as Duke of Jin, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 趙貴、獨孤信等將謀襲護，護因貴入朝，執之，黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui, Dugu Xin, and others plotted to attack Hu; when Gui entered court, Hu seized him; accomplices were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui, Dugu Xin, and others plotted to attack Yuwen Hu; when Zhao Gui entered court, Hu seized him; accomplices were all executed.

sentences.zh: 拜大塚宰。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時司會李植、軍司馬孫恆等密要宮伯乙弗鳳、張光洛、賀拔提、元進等為腹心，說帝，言護不守臣節，宜圖之。

translations.literal: At the time Director of Audits Li Zhi, army secretary Sun Heng, and others secretly recruited palace guards Yifu Feng, Zhang Guangluo, Heba Ti, and Yuan Jin as confidants, spoke to the emperor, and said Hu did not keep minister's conduct and should be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of Audits Li Zhi, army secretary Sun Heng, and others secretly recruited palace guards Yifu Feng, Zhang Guangluo, Heba Ti, and Yuan Jin as confidants, told the emperor that Yuwen Hu did not keep a minister's conduct, and urged that he be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，數將武士于後園，為執縛勢。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; he repeatedly led warriors in the rear garden in the posture of binding and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; he repeatedly led warriors in the rear garden to drill in the posture of binding and seizing.

sentences.zh: 護微知之。

translations.literal: Hu slightly knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu had some inkling of it.

sentences.zh: 出植為梁州，恆為潼州，欲遏其謀。

translations.literal: He sent Zhi out as governor of Liang Province and Heng out as governor of Tong Province, wishing to check their plot.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Zhi out as governor of Liang Province and Sun Heng out as governor of Tong Province, wishing to check their plot.

sentences.zh: 後帝思植等，每欲召之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor missed Zhi and the others and often wished to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor missed Li Zhi and the others and often wished to summon them.

sentences.zh: 護諫曰：「天下至親，不過兄弟。

translations.literal: Hu remonstrated, saying: "The closest kin under Heaven is nothing beyond brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu remonstrated, saying: "The closest kin under Heaven is nothing beyond brothers.

sentences.zh: 若兄弟自構嫌隙，他人何易可親？

translations.literal: If brothers themselves build suspicion and rifts, how easily can others be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: If brothers themselves build suspicion and rifts, how easily can others be trusted?.

sentences.zh: 但恐除臣後，奸回得逞其欲，非唯不處陛下，亦危社稷。」

translations.literal: But I fear that after removing me, wicked men will achieve their desires—not only failing to serve Your Majesty, but also endangering the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that after I am removed, treacherous men will have their way—not only failing to serve Your Majesty properly, but also endangering the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 因泣涕，久之乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept tears; only after long did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wept; only after long did he stop.

sentences.zh: 帝猶猜，鳳等益懼，密謀滋甚，遂克日將誅護。

translations.literal: The emperor still suspected him. Feng and the others grew all the more afraid; secret plotting grew ever deeper. They thereupon set a day when they would execute Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still suspected him. Yifu Feng and the others grew all the more afraid, and their secret plotting intensified until they fixed a day to kill Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 光洛告護，護乃召柱國賀蘭祥、小司馬尉遲綱等以鳳謀告之。

translations.literal: Guangluo fully reported their earlier and later plot to Hu; Hu thereupon summoned Pillar-of-State Helan Xiang, junior marshal Yuchi Gang, and others, and told them of Feng's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangluo fully reported their earlier and later plot to Yuwen Hu; Yuwen Hu thereupon summoned Pillar-of-State Helan Xiang, junior marshal Yuchi Gang, and others, and told them of Yifu Feng's plot.

sentences.zh: 祥並勸廢帝。

translations.literal: Xiang and the others all urged Hu to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Xiang and the others all urged Yuwen Hu to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時綱總領禁兵，護乃遣綱入宮，召鳳等議事，以次執送護第。

translations.literal: At the time Gang commanded the forbidden troops; Hu thereupon sent Gang into the palace to summon Feng and the others to discuss affairs, and when they came out, seized them in order and sent them to Hu's residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuchi Gang commanded the forbidden troops; Yuwen Hu thereupon sent Gang into the palace to summon Feng and the others to discuss affairs, and when they came out, seized them in order and sent them to Yuwen Hu's residence.

sentences.zh: 因罷散宿衛兵，遣祥逼帝，幽于舊邸。

translations.literal: He thereupon dismissed and dispersed the night-guard troops, sent Xiang to compel the emperor, and confined him in the old residence.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon dismissed and dispersed the night-guard troops, sent Helan Xiang to compel the emperor, and confined him in the old residence.

sentences.zh: 於是召公卿畢集護第。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all nobles and ministers to assemble at Hu's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yuwen Hu summoned all the nobles and ministers to assemble at his residence.

sentences.zh: 護曰：「先王勤勞王業三十餘年，寇賊未平，奄棄萬國。

translations.literal: Hu said: "The late king toiled at the royal enterprise for more than thirty years; bandits and enemies were not yet pacified when suddenly he abandoned the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu said: "The late king toiled at the royal enterprise for more than thirty years; bandits and enemies were not yet pacified when suddenly he abandoned the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 寡人地則猶子，親受顧命，以略陽公既居正嫡，與公等立而奉之，革魏興周，為四海主。

translations.literal: I in status am like a younger son and personally received the deathbed charge; because Duke of Lueyang already held the legitimate succession, with you nobles we established and served him, changed Wei and raised Zhou, and made him master of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I in status was like a younger son and personally received the deathbed charge; because the Duke of Lueyang already held the legitimate succession, together with you gentlemen we enthroned and served him, replaced Wei with Zhou, and made him sovereign of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 自即位已來，荒淫無度，昵近群小，疏忌骨肉，大臣重將，咸欲誅夷。

translations.literal: Since ascending the throne he has been dissolute without measure, intimate with petty men, distant and jealous of kin, and great ministers and important generals—all wished to be executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Since ascending the throne he has been dissolute without measure, intimate with petty men, distant and jealous of kin, and great ministers and important generals—all wished to be executed and destroyed — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 若此謀遂行，社稷必致傾覆。

translations.literal: If this plot had been carried out, the altars of state would surely have been overturned.
translations.idiomatic: If this plot had been carried out, the altars of state would surely have been overturned — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 寡人若死，將何面目以見先王？

translations.literal: If I die, with what face could I see the late king?
translations.idiomatic: If I die, with what face could I see the late king?.

sentences.zh: 今日甯負略陽公，豈可負社稷！

translations.literal: Today I would rather fail Duke of Lueyang than fail the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Today I would rather fail Duke of Lueyang than fail the altars of state — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 寧都公年德兼茂，仁孝聖慈，今欲廢昏立明，公等以為何如？」

translations.literal: Duke of Ning in years and virtue is abundant together, benevolent, filial, sage, and compassionate; now we wish to depose the dark and establish the bright—what do you nobles think?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ning is mature in years and virtue, benevolent, filial, and sage-like; we now wish to depose the unworthy ruler and establish a worthy one—what do you gentlemen think?

sentences.zh: 群公咸曰：「此公之家事，敢不唯命是聽！」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all said: "This is your Grace's family affair—we dare not but obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers all said: "This is your Grace's family affair—we dare not but obey your command.".

sentences.zh: 於是斬鳳等於門外，並誅植、恆。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng and the others were beheaded outside the gate; Zhi, Heng, and the others were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yifu Feng and the others were beheaded outside the gate; Li Zhi, Sun Heng, and the others were also executed.

sentences.zh: 尋弑帝，迎明帝於岐州而立之。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor was also assassinated; they welcomed Emperor Ming from Qi Province and established him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they assassinated the emperor and welcomed Emperor Ming from Qi Province to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜太師，賜路車冕服，封子至為崇業郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed grand preceptor, granted carriage and court robes, and his son Zhi was enfeoffed as Duke of Chongye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yuwen Hu was appointed Grand Preceptor, granted carriage and court robes, and his son Zhi was enfeoffed as Duke of Chongye commandery.

sentences.zh: 初改雍州刺史為牧，以護為之，並賜金石之東。

translations.literal: When the governor of Yong Province was first changed to governor-general, Hu was made such and was also granted stone-and-metal music.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of governor of Yong Province was first changed to governor-general, Yuwen Hu was appointed to it and was also granted the stone-and-metal orchestra.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，護上表政，帝許之，軍國大事尚委於護。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, Hu submitted a memorial returning government; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng (559), Yuwen Hu submitted a memorial returning government; the emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝性聰睿，有識量，護深憚之。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was clever and perceptive, with judgment and capacity; Hu deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature was clever and perceptive, with judgment and capacity; Yuwen Hu deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 有李安者，本以鼎俎得寵於護，擢為膳部下大夫。

translations.literal: There was one Li An who originally through kitchen service gained Hu's favor; gradually he was promoted and reached the post of lower grandee of the victuals ministry.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Li An who originally through kitchen service gained Yuwen Hu's favor; gradually he was promoted and reached the post of lower grandee of the victuals ministry.

sentences.zh: 至是，護令安因進食加毒，帝遂崩。

translations.literal: At this time Hu secretly ordered An, when presenting food to the emperor, to add poison.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yuwen Hu secretly ordered Li An, when presenting food to the emperor, to add poison.

sentences.zh: 護立武帝，百官總已以聽護。

translations.literal: Hu established Emperor Wu; the hundred officials all turned to themselves and took orders from Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu enthroned Emperor Wu (Yuwen Yong); all officials deferred to Yuwen Hu in governing.

sentences.zh: 先是，護母閻與皇第四姑及諸戚屬並沒齊，皆被幽縶。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hu's mother Lady Yan and the imperial fourth aunt and various kin, all were captured in Northern Qi and were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuwen Hu's mother Lady Yan and the imperial fourth aunt and various kin, all were captured in Northern Qi and were all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 護居宰相後，每遣間使尋求，莫知音息。

translations.literal: After Hu held the chancellor's post, he repeatedly sent secret envoys to seek them; no word of their fate was heard.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu held the chancellor's post, he repeatedly sent secret envoys to seek them; no word of their fate was heard.

sentences.zh: 至是，並許還朝，且請和好。

translations.literal: At this time all were permitted to return to court and also sought reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: At this time all were permitted to return to court and Northern Qi also sought reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 四年，皇姑先至。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the imperial aunt arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the imperial aunt arrived first — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 齊主以護權重，乃留其母，以為後圖。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi ruler, because Hu already held heavy power, thereupon detained his mother as a plan for later.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler, because Yuwen Hu already held heavy power, thereupon detained his mother as a plan for later.

sentences.zh: 仍令人為閻作書與護曰：

translations.literal: He still had someone write a letter for Lady Yan reporting to Hu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He still had someone write a letter for Lady Yan reporting to Yuwen Hu, saying:

sentences.zh: 吾念十九入汝家，今以八十矣。

translations.literal: I myself recall entering your household at nineteen; now I am already eighty.
translations.idiomatic: I myself recall entering your household at nineteen; now I am already eighty — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 凡生汝輩三男二女，今日目下，不睹一人，興言及此，悲纏肌骨。

translations.literal: In all I bore you three sons and two daughters; today before my eyes I do not see a single one. Speaking of this, grief binds muscle and bone.
translations.idiomatic: In all I bore you three sons and two daughters; today before my eyes I do not see a single one. To speak of this binds grief into my very bones.

sentences.zh: 賴皇齊恩恤，差安衰暮。

translations.literal: Relying on Great Qi's gracious pity, I am somewhat at ease in my declining years.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Great Qi's gracious pity, I am somewhat at ease in my declining years — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 又得與汝楊氏姑及汝叔母紇幹、汝嫂劉及汝新婦等同居，頗以自適。

translations.literal: I also have your Yang paternal aunt and your uncle's wife Hegan and your sister-in-law Lady Liu Xinfu and others living together; it is also rather comfortable.
translations.idiomatic: I also have your Yang paternal aunt and your uncle's wife Hegan and your sister-in-law Lady Liu Xinfu and others living together; it is also rather comfortable — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 但為微有耳疾，大語方聞，行動飲食，幸無多損。

translations.literal: Only I have slight ear ailment; only loud speech can be heard. In movement and in eating and drinking, fortunately there is not much harm.
translations.idiomatic: I only have a slight ear ailment and can hear only when speech is loud; in moving about and in eating and drinking, fortunately I suffer little impairment.

sentences.zh: 汝與吾別之時，年尚幼小，以前家事，或不委曲。

translations.literal: When you parted from me, you were still young; regarding earlier household affairs, perhaps you do not know the full details.
translations.idiomatic: When you parted from me, you were still young; regarding earlier household affairs, perhaps you do not know the full details — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 昔在武川鎮，生汝兄弟，大才屬鼠，第二屬兔，汝身屬蛇。

translations.literal: Formerly at Wuchuan garrison your brothers were born—the eldest belongs to the rat, the next to the rabbit, and you yourself to the snake.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at Wuchuan garrison your brothers were born—the eldest belongs to the rat, the next to the rabbit, and you yourself to the snake — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 鮮于修禮起日，吾闔家大小先在博陵郡住，相將欲向左人城。

translations.literal: On the day Xianyu Xiuli rose, my whole household large and small was first living in Boling commandery; we were about to go together toward Zuoren city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xianyu Xiuli rose in rebellion, my whole household, great and small, was then living in Boling commandery and was about to set out together for Zuoren city.

sentences.zh: 至唐河北，被定州官軍打敗。

translations.literal: We were about to go together toward Zuoren city; when we reached north of the Tang River, we were defeated by Ding Province government troops.
translations.idiomatic: We were about to go together toward Zuoren city; when we reached north of the Tang River, we were defeated by Ding Province government troops — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 汝祖及第二叔時俱戰亡。

translations.literal: Your grandfather and two uncles at the time all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfather and two uncles at the time all died in battle — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 叔母賀拔及兒元寶、汝叔母紇幹及兒菩提並吾與汝六人，同被禽捉入定州城。

translations.literal: Your uncle's wife Heba and son Yuanbao, your uncle's wife Hegan and son Puti, together with me and you six people, were all captured and taken into Ding Province city.
translations.idiomatic: Your uncle's wife Heba and son Yuanbao, your uncle's wife Hegan and son Puti, together with me and you six people, were all captured and taken into Ding Province city — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 未幾間，將吾及汝送與元寶掌，賀拔、紇幹各別分散。

translations.literal: Before long they sent me and you to Yuanbao's custody; Heba and Hegan each separately dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they handed me and you over to Yuanbao's custody, while Heba and Hegan were each sent away separately.

sentences.zh: 寶掌軍營在唐城內，經停三日。

translations.literal: Baozhang's army camp was inside Tang city and halted there three days.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhang's army encamped inside Tang city and remained there three days.

sentences.zh: 寶掌所掠得男夫女婦可六七千人，悉送向京。

translations.literal: After stopping three days, the men and women Baozhang had plundered, about sixty or seventy people, were all sent toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After stopping three days, the men and women Baozhang had plundered, about sixty or seventy people, were all sent toward the capital — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 吾時與汝同被送限。

translations.literal: At the time I and you were sent together under guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time I and you were sent together under guard — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 至定州城南，夜宿同鄉人姬庫根家。

translations.literal: Reaching south of Ding Province city, at night we lodged at fellow townsman Ji Kugen's house.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching south of Ding Province city, at night we lodged at fellow townsman Ji Kugen's house — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕奴望見鮮于修禮營火。

translations.literal: Ruru slave saw Xianyu Xiuli's camp fires and said to me: "I now will go toward the main army."
translations.idiomatic: Ruru slave saw Xianyu Xiuli's camp fires and said to me: "I now will go toward the main army.".

sentences.zh: 語吾云：「今走向本軍。」

translations.literal: He said to me: "Now I will go toward our original army.
translations.idiomatic: He said to me: "Now I will go back to our original army.

sentences.zh: 既至營，遂告吾輩在此。

translations.literal: When he reached the camp, he thereupon reported that we were here.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the camp, he thereupon reported that we were here — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 明旦日出，汝叔將兵邀截，吾及汝等還得向營。

translations.literal: The next morning at sunrise your uncle led troops to intercept; I and you and the others were able to return toward the camp.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning at sunrise your uncle led troops to intercept; I and you and the others were able to return toward the camp.

sentences.zh: 汝時年十二，共吾並乘馬隨軍，可不記此事由緣也？

translations.literal: You at the time were twelve; together with me you both rode horses following the army—you surely remember this matter's origin, do you not?
translations.idiomatic: You at the time were twelve; together with me you both rode horses following the army—you surely remember this matter's origin, do you not?.

sentences.zh: 後吾共汝在壽陽任。

translations.literal: Afterward I and you lived at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward I and you lived at Shouyang — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 時元寶、菩提及汝姑兒賀蘭盛洛，並汝身四人同學。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanbao, Puti, and your aunt's son Helan Shenglo, together with you yourself, four people studied together.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanbao, Puti, and your aunt's son Helan Shenglo, together with you yourself, four people studied together — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 博士姓成，為人嚴惡，汝等四人謀欲加害。

translations.literal: The instructor surnamed Cheng was by nature stern and harsh; you four plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor surnamed Cheng was stern and harsh by nature; the four of you plotted to harm him.

sentences.zh: 吾共汝叔母聞知，各捉其兒打之。

translations.literal: I and your uncles' wives and others heard of it; each seized her son and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: I and your uncles' wives and others heard of it; each seized her son and beat him — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 唯盛洛無母，獨不被打。

translations.literal: Only Shenglo had no mother; alone he was not beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shenglo had no mother; alone he was not beaten — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 後爾硃天柱亡歲，賀拔阿斗泥在關西，遣人迎家累。

translations.literal: Afterward, in the year Erzhu Tianzhu died, Heba Adouni was in Guanxi and sent men to welcome family dependents.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, in the year Erzhu Tianzhu died, Heba Adouni was in Guanxi and sent men to welcome family dependents — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 汝叔亦遣奴來富迎汝及盛洛等。

translations.literal: At the time your uncle also sent a slave named Laifu to welcome you and Shenglo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At the time your uncle also sent a slave named Laifu to welcome you and Shenglo and the others — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 汝時著緋綾袍、銀裝帶，盛洛著紫纖成纈通身袍，黃綾裏，並乘騾同去。

translations.literal: You at the time wore a crimson gauze robe and silver-decorated belt; Shenglo wore a purple woven patterned robe over the whole body with yellow gauze lining; you both rode mules and went together.
translations.idiomatic: You at the time wore a crimson gauze robe and silver-decorated belt; Shenglo wore a purple woven patterned robe over the whole body with yellow gauze lining; you both rode mules and went together — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 盛洛小於汝，三人並喚吾作阿摩敦。

translations.literal: Shenglo was younger than you; you three all called me "Amodun."
translations.idiomatic: Shenglo was younger than you; you three all called me "Amodun.".

sentences.zh: 如此之事，當分明記之。

translations.literal: Matters like this—you should clearly remember them.
translations.idiomatic: Matters like this—you should clearly remember them — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 今又寄汝小時所著錦袍表一領，至宜撿看，知吾含悲抱戚，多歷年祀。

translations.literal: Now I also send you the brocade robe with facing you wore in childhood, one piece; when it arrives you should inspect it and know my grief and sorrow have lasted many years.
translations.idiomatic: Now I also send you the brocade robe with facing you wore in childhood, one piece; when it arrives you should inspect it and know my grief and sorrow have lasted many years — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 禽獸草木，母子相依，吾有何罪，與汝分隔，今復何福，還望見汝。

translations.literal: Birds and beasts and plants and trees—mother and child rely on each other; what crime have I that I am separated from you; what blessing now that I again may hope to see you?
translations.idiomatic: Birds and beasts and plants and trees—mother and child rely on each other; what crime have I that I am separated from you; what blessing now that I again may hope to see you?.

sentences.zh: 世間所有，求皆可得，母子異國，何處可求！

translations.literal: All that exists in the world, if sought, can all be obtained; mother and son in different states—where can it be sought?
translations.idiomatic: All that exists in the world, if sought, can all be obtained; mother and son in different states—where can it be sought?.

sentences.zh: 假汝貴極公王，富過山海；

translations.literal: Suppose you were noble to the utmost of kings and dukes, rich beyond mountains and seas;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose you were noble to the utmost of kings and dukes, rich beyond mountains and seas;.

sentences.zh: 有一老母，八十之年，飄在千里，死亡旦夕，不得一朝暫見，不得一日同處，寒不得汝衣，饑不得汝食，汝雖窮榮極盛，光耀世間，汝何用為？

translations.literal: There is one old mother, eighty years, adrift a thousand li, death morning and evening, unable to obtain one morning's brief sight, unable one day to dwell together; cold yet not your clothes, hungry yet not your food—you though exhausted in glory and utmost splendor, shining over the world, of what use are you?
translations.idiomatic: There is an old mother of eighty, cast a thousand li away, with death imminent, unable to see you even once, unable to share a single day under one roof—cold without your garment, hungry without your food; though you were exalted to the utmost in rank and glory, shining over the world, what good is that to me?

sentences.zh: 于吾何益？

translations.literal: What benefit to me?
translations.idiomatic: What benefit to me?.

sentences.zh: 吾今日之前，汝既不得申其供養，事往何論。

translations.literal: Before today you already could not perform your support; what is past, what need to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Before today you already could not perform your support; what is past, what need to discuss — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 今日以後，吾之殘命，唯系於汝。

translations.literal: From today onward my remaining life is only bound to you.
translations.idiomatic: From today onward my remaining life depends entirely on you.

sentences.zh: 戴天履地，中有鬼神，勿雲冥昧，而可欺負。

translations.literal: From today afterward my remaining life is only bound to you; you tread Heaven and stand on earth—within are ghosts and spirits; do not say darkness and obscurity and so may be deceived and wronged.
translations.idiomatic: From today afterward my remaining life is only bound to you; you tread Heaven and stand on earth—within are ghosts and spirits; do not say darkness and obscurity and so may be deceived and wronged — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 楊氏姑今雖炎暑，猶能先發。

translations.literal: Your Yang paternal aunt, though now it is blazing summer, still can set out first.
translations.idiomatic: Your Yang paternal aunt, though now it is blazing summer, still can set out first — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 關、河阻遠，隔絕多年，書依常體，慮汝致惑，是以每存款質，兼亦載吾姓名，當識此理，勿以為怪。

translations.literal: Passes and rivers are blocked and far; separated many years; letters follow ordinary form; fearing you would be confused, therefore each time I add pledges and proofs and also record my name—you should understand this principle and not regard it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Passes and rivers lie far apart and we have been cut off for many years; the letter follows the usual form, but fearing you might be puzzled I therefore add pledges each time and also give my name—you should understand this and not find it strange.

sentences.zh: 護性至孝，得書悲不自勝，左右莫能仰視。

translations.literal: Hu by nature was supremely filial; receiving the letter, grief could not be overcome; those at his side none could look up.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu by nature was supremely filial; receiving the letter, grief could not be overcome; those at his side none could look up.

sentences.zh: 報書云：

translations.literal: His reply letter said:
translations.idiomatic: His reply letter said:.

sentences.zh: 區宇分崩，遭遇災禍，違離膝下，三十五年。

translations.literal: The realm split and collapsed; I encountered disaster and calamity; parted from beneath your knees thirty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: The realm split and collapsed; I encountered disaster and calamity; parted from beneath your knees thirty-five years.

sentences.zh: 受形稟氣，皆知母子，誰知薩保，如此不孝！

translations.literal: Receiving form and inheriting breath, all know mother and son—who like Saba is so unfilial!
translations.idiomatic: Receiving form and inheriting breath, all know mother and son—who like Saba is so unfilial!.

sentences.zh: 宿殃積戾，唯應賜鍾，豈悟綱羅，上嬰慈母。

translations.literal: Accumulated misfortune and piled guilt—only death should be granted; who expected the net and snare would reach up to afflict my compassionate mother.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated misfortune and piled guilt—only death should be granted; who expected the net and snare would reach up to afflict my compassionate mother — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 但立身立行，不負一物，明神有識，宜先哀憐。

translations.literal: But in establishing body and establishing conduct I have not failed a single thing; the bright spirits have knowledge—they should see pity.
translations.idiomatic: But in establishing body and establishing conduct I have not failed a single thing; the bright spirits have knowledge—they should see pity — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 而子為公侯，母為俘隸，熱不見母熱，寒不見母寒，衣不知有無，食不知饑飽，泯如天地之外，無由暫聞。

translations.literal: Yet the son is duke and marquis while the mother is captive slave; hot yet not seeing mother's heat, cold yet not seeing mother's cold; clothes not knowing whether there are any, food not knowing hunger or fullness—vanished as beyond Heaven and earth, without means briefly to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the son is duke and marquis while the mother is captive slave; hot yet not seeing mother's heat, cold yet not seeing mother's cold; clothes not knowing whether there are any, food not knowing hunger or fullness—vanished as beyond Heaven and earth, without means briefly to hear — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 晝夜悲號，繼之以血，分懷冤酷，終此一生，死若有知，冀奉見於泉下耳。

translations.literal: Day and night wailing, continuing with blood; parting harbors bitter cruelty—through this one life; if death has knowledge, I hope to serve and see you beneath the springs.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night wailing, continuing with blood; parting harbors bitter cruelty—through this one life; if death has knowledge, I hope to serve and see you beneath the springs — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 不謂齊朝解綱，惠以德音，摩敦、四姑，並許哀放。

translations.literal: I did not expect Northern Qi court would release the net, grace with virtuous word; Modun and the fourth aunt were all permitted compassionate release.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect Northern Qi court would release the net, grace with virtuous word; Modun and the fourth aunt were all permitted compassionate release — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 初聞此旨，魂爽飛越，號天叩地，不能自勝。

translations.literal: On first hearing this intent, soul and spirit flew and leaped; I cried to Heaven and knocked on earth and could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: On first hearing this intent, soul and spirit flew and leaped; I cried to Heaven and knocked on earth and could not overcome — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 四姑即蒙禮送，平安入境，以今月十八日於河東拜見。

translations.literal: The fourth aunt immediately received ceremonial escort, peacefully entered the border; on the eighteenth of this month at Hedong I paid respects and saw her.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth aunt immediately received ceremonial escort, peacefully entered the border; on the eighteenth of this month at Hedong I paid respects and saw her.

sentences.zh: 遙奉顏色，崩慟肝腸。

translations.literal: From afar receiving her countenance, liver and intestines collapsed and shook.
translations.idiomatic: From afar receiving her countenance, liver and intestines collapsed and shook — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 但離絕多年，存亡阻隔，相見之始，口未忍言。

translations.literal: But separated many years, life and death blocked; at the beginning of meeting, the mouth could not bear to speak.
translations.idiomatic: But after years of separation and the barrier between life and death, at the first meeting I could not bear to speak.

sentences.zh: 唯敘齊朝寬弘，每存大德，雲與摩敦雖處宮禁，常蒙優禮，今者來鄴，恩遇彌隆。

translations.literal: She said that though Modun was in palace confinement, he constantly received generous rites; now coming to Ye, gracious treatment was ever more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: She said that though Modun was in palace confinement, he constantly received generous rites; now coming to Ye, gracious treatment was ever more abundant — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 重降矜哀，聽許摩敦垂敕，曲盡悲酷，備述家事。

translations.literal: Pitying and hearing permission for Modun to send down command, fully narrating bitter cruelty, fully relating household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying and hearing permission for Modun to send down command, fully narrating bitter cruelty, fully relating household affairs — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 伏讀未周，五情屠割。

translations.literal: Humbly reading, not yet finished, the five emotions were butchered and cut.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly reading, not yet finished, the five emotions were butchered and cut — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 書中所道，無一事敢忘。

translations.literal: What the letter stated—no matter I dare forget.
translations.idiomatic: What the letter stated—no matter I dare forget — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 摩敦年尊，又加憂苦，常謂寢食貶損，或多遺漏。

translations.literal: Modun is advanced in years and again added worry and suffering; I often supposed sleep and meals were diminished or many omissions;
translations.idiomatic: Modun is advanced in years and again added worry and suffering; I often supposed sleep and meals were diminished or many omissions;.

sentences.zh: 伏奉論述，次第分明。

translations.literal: humbly receiving your narration, sequence clear and distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly receiving your narration, sequence clear and distinct.

sentences.zh: 一則以悲，一則以喜。

translations.literal: One part grief, one part joy.
translations.idiomatic: One part grief, one part joy — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 當鄉里破敗之日，薩保年以十餘歲，鄰曲舊事，猶自記憶；

translations.literal: When the hometown was broken and ruined, Saba was already more than ten years; neighborhood old affairs still himself remembers;
translations.idiomatic: When the hometown was broken and ruined, Saba was already more than ten years; neighborhood old affairs still himself remembers;.

sentences.zh: 況家門禍難，親戚流離？

translations.literal: How much more household disaster and difficulty, kin scattered in exile?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so the calamities at our family gate and the scattering of our kin in exile?

sentences.zh: 奉辭時節，先後慈訓，刻肌刻骨，常纏心府。

translations.literal: how much more household gate disaster and difficulty, kin scattered and displaced, times of parting words, earlier and later compassionate instruction—carved in flesh and carved in bone, constantly binding heart and bowels.
translations.idiomatic: How much more household gate disaster and difficulty, kin scattered and displaced, times of parting words, earlier and later compassionate instruction—carved in flesh and carved in bone, constantly binding heart and bowels.

sentences.zh: 天長喪亂，四海橫流，太祖乘時，齊朝撫運，兩河三輔，各遇神機。

translations.literal: Heaven long in turmoil and ruin; the four seas flow crosswise; the Grand Progenitor seized the time; Northern Qi court received the mandate; the two rivers and three auxiliaries each met divine opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven endured long ages of chaos and the four seas were swept by turmoil; the Grand Progenitor seized the moment, the Northern Qi court received the mandate, and the two capitals and three auxiliaries each met their destined opening.

sentences.zh: 源其事蹟，非相負背。

translations.literal: Examining the matter's traces, it was not mutual betrayal.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the matter's traces, it was not mutual betrayal — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 太祖升遐，未定薩保，薩保屬當猶子之長，親受顧命。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ascended to the distant; Sabao was not yet settled; Sabao happened to be eldest among younger sons and personally received the deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai passed away, the post of Sabao had not yet been fixed; Sabao happened to be the eldest among the younger sons and personally received the final charge.

sentences.zh: 雖身居重任，職當憂責，至於歲時稱慶，子孫在庭，顧視悲摧，心情斷絕，胡顏履戴，負愧神明。

translations.literal: Though body held heavy responsibility and office bore worry and blame, as to seasonal celebrations with descendants in the hall, looking back grief crushed, heart and feelings severed, shameful face treading Heaven and standing on earth, bearing guilt before the bright spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Though I bear heavy responsibility and the duties of office bring worry and blame, when the seasons call for celebration and descendants gather in the hall, I look back in crushing grief and my heart is torn apart; how can I face Heaven and earth without shame, or bear my guilt before the spirits?

sentences.zh: 齊朝霈然之恩，既已沾洽，愛敬之至，施及傍人。

translations.literal: Northern Qi court sudden rain-like grace already has soaked through; utmost love and reverence extend even to those beside.
translations.idiomatic: The sudden, sweeping grace of the Northern Qi court has already reached us fully; the utmost love and reverence extend even to those standing beside us.

sentences.zh: 草木有心，禽魚感澤，況在人倫，而不銘戴？

translations.literal: Plants and trees have hearts; birds and fish feel the marsh; how much more in human relations—not to inscribe and bear on the head?
translations.idiomatic: Plants and trees have hearts; birds and fish feel kindness; how much more among human bonds—how could we fail to inscribe it and bear it upon our heads?

sentences.zh: 有國有家，信義為本，伏度來期，已應有日。

translations.literal: Having state and having family, faith and righteousness are the root; humbly calculating the coming date, already there should be a day.
translations.idiomatic: For those who hold a state and a household, faith and righteousness are the foundation; humbly reckoning the day of your return, it ought already to be near.

sentences.zh: 一得奉見慈顏，永畢生願。

translations.literal: Once obtaining to serve and see your compassionate countenance, forever completing life's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Once obtaining to serve and see your compassionate countenance, forever completing life's wish — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 生死肉骨，豈過今恩，負山戴嶽，未足勝荷。

translations.literal: Death and life flesh and bone—how could it surpass today's grace; bearing mountains and wearing peaks—not enough to overcome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: To restore life to the dead and flesh to bone—what could surpass this grace of today? Bearing mountains on my back and wearing peaks on my head would not be enough to repay it.

sentences.zh: 二國分隔，理無書信，主上以彼朝不絕母子之恩，亦賜許奉答。

translations.literal: The two states are separated; by principle there are no letters; the sovereign because that court did not cut off mother-son affection also granted permission to send reply.
translations.idiomatic: The two states are divided, and by principle there should be no correspondence; yet our sovereign, because that court did not sever the bond between mother and son, also granted permission to send a reply.

sentences.zh: 不期今日，得通家問，伏紙嗚咽，言不宣心。

translations.literal: I did not expect today to obtain communication of family news; humbly before the paper I sob and choke; words cannot express the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect today to obtain communication of family news; humbly before the paper I sob and choke; words cannot express the heart — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 蒙寄薩保別時所留錦袍表，年歲雖久，宛然猶識，抱此悲泣，至於拜見，事歸忍死，知復何心！

translations.literal: Receiving the brocade robe and collar Sabao left when parting, though years have passed I still recognize them clearly; holding them I weep in grief; as for bowing and meeting face to face, the matter comes down to enduring life—what heart can I have left!
translations.idiomatic: You also sent the brocade robe and collar you had left when Sabao parted; though many years have passed, I still recognize them at once, and holding them I weep in grief. As for bowing and meeting you in person, I must simply endure and live on—what heart can I have after that!

sentences.zh: 齊朝不即發遣，更令重與護書，要護重報。

translations.literal: Northern Qi did not send her off at once, but again had her exchange letters with Hu, requiring Hu to reply again.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi did not send her off at once, but had her exchange letters with Yuwen Hu again, demanding a further reply from him.

sentences.zh: 護復書，往返至於再三，而母竟不至。

translations.literal: Hu replied in letters; back and forth several times, yet his mother still did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu wrote back; after several rounds of correspondence, his mother still did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 朝議以其失信，令有司移齊，移未送而母至。

translations.literal: The court, holding that they had broken faith, ordered the offices to address Qi; the letter had not yet been sent when the mother arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The court, judging them faithless, ordered the offices to send a letter to Qi; the letter had not yet been sent when his mother arrived.

sentences.zh: 舉朝慶悅，大赦天下。

translations.literal: The whole court rejoiced, and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court rejoiced, and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 護與母暌隔多年，一朝聚集，凡所資奉，窮極華盛。

translations.literal: Hu and his mother had been separated many years; once gathered, all that was supplied and served reached the utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu and his mother had been separated many years; once reunited, all that was supplied and served reached the utmost splendor.

sentences.zh: 每四時伏臘，武帝率諸親戚，行家人禮，稱觴上壽，榮貴之極，振古未聞。

translations.literal: At each season's fasting day and year-end sacrifice, Emperor Wu led the kinsmen in family rites, raising cups and offering long life—glory and honor at the extreme, unheard of since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At each seasonal fast and year-end sacrifice, Emperor Yuwen Yong led the kinsmen in family rites, raising cups and offering long life—glory and honor at the extreme, unheard of since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 護性甚寬和，然暗於大體。

translations.literal: Hu's nature was very mild and harmonious, yet he was dim regarding the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's nature was very mild and harmonious, yet he was dim regarding the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 自恃建立功，久當權軸，所任皆非其人。

translations.literal: Relying on his merit in establishment, he long held the pivot of power; all whom he entrusted were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his achievements at the founding, he long held the pivot of power; none of those he appointed were the right men.

sentences.zh: 兼諸子貪殘，僚屬縱溢，莫不蠹政害人。

translations.literal: Moreover his sons were greedy and cruel, his staff unrestrained; none failed to corrupt government and harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his sons were greedy and cruel and his subordinates ran wild; none failed to corrupt government and harm the people.

sentences.zh: 以其暴慢，密與衛王直圖之。

translations.literal: Because of his arrogance and insolence, the emperor secretly plotted with Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi against him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his arrogance and insolence, Emperor Yuwen Yong secretly plotted with Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi against him.

sentences.zh: 七年三月十八日，護自同州還，帝御文安殿見護訖，引入含仁殿，朝皇太后。

translations.literal: Seventh year, third month, eighteenth day, Hu returned from Tong Province; the emperor attended at Wen'an Hall, and when he had seen Hu, led him into Hanren Hall to attend upon the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, third month, eighteenth day, Yuwen Hu returned from Tong Province; the emperor received him at Wen'an Hall, and when the audience was finished, led him into Hanren Hall to attend upon the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝於禁中見護，常行家人禮。

translations.literal: Before this, when the emperor saw Hu within the forbidden precinct, he always observed family rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when the emperor saw Yuwen Hu within the palace, he always observed family rites.

sentences.zh: 護謁太后，太后必賜之坐，帝每立侍。

translations.literal: When Hu attended upon the Empress Dowager, she always granted him a seat, and the emperor each time stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu attended upon the Empress Dowager, she always granted him a seat, and the emperor each time stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 至是，護將入，帝謂曰：「太后春秋既尊，頗好酒，諸親朝謁，或廢引進。

translations.literal: At this, as Hu was about to enter, the emperor said to him: "The Empress Dowager's years are already advanced, and she greatly loves wine; when kinsmen attend court audiences, sometimes reception is omitted.
translations.idiomatic: At this, as Yuwen Hu was about to enter, the emperor said to him: "The Empress Dowager's years are already advanced, and she greatly loves wine; when kinsmen attend court audiences, sometimes reception is omitted.

sentences.zh: 喜怒有時乖爽。

translations.literal: Between joy and anger there are at times departures from propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Between joy and anger there are at times departures from propriety — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 比諫，未蒙垂納。

translations.literal: Recently I remonstrated but was not granted acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I remonstrated but was not granted acceptance — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 兄今願更啟請。」

translations.literal: Elder brother, now that you are attending court, I wish you would raise the matter again."
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother, now that you are attending court, I wish you would raise the matter again — so the record states."

sentences.zh: 因出懷中酒誥授護曰：「以此諫太后。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the "Admonition on Wine" from his bosom and gave it to Hu, saying: "Use this to remonstrate with the Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took the "Admonition on Wine" from his bosom and gave it to Yuwen Hu, saying: "Use this to remonstrate with the Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 護入，如帝所誡，讀示太后。

translations.literal: Hu having entered, as the emperor had instructed, read and showed it to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu having entered, as the emperor had instructed, read and showed it to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 未訖，帝以玉珽自後擊之，踣地，又令宦者何泉以禦刀斫之。

translations.literal: Before he finished, the emperor struck him from behind with a jade tablet, and he fell to the ground; he also ordered the eunuch He Quan to hack at him with the imperial blade.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor struck him from behind with a jade tablet, and Yuwen Hu fell to the ground; he also ordered the eunuch He Quan to hack at him with the imperial blade.

sentences.zh: 泉懼，斫不能傷。

translations.literal: He Quan in fear hacked but could not wound him.
translations.idiomatic: He Quan, in fear, hacked but could not wound him.

sentences.zh: 時衛王直先匿於戶內，乃出斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Wei Zhi had first hidden inside the door, then came out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi had first hidden inside the door, then came out and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 初，帝欲圖護，王軌、宇文神舉、宇文孝伯頗預其謀。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor wished to plot against Hu, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, and Yuwen Xiaobo had all taken part in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the emperor wished to plot against Yuwen Hu, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, and Yuwen Xiaobo had all taken part in the plan.

sentences.zh: 是日，軌等並在外，更無知者。

translations.literal: That day, Gui and the others were all outside, and no one else knew.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Wang Gui and the others were all outside, and no one else knew.

sentences.zh: 殺護訖，乃召宮伯長孫覽等，即令收護子柱國譚國公會、大將軍莒國公至、崇業公靜、正平公乾嘉及乾基、乾蔚、乾祖、乾威等，並柱國侯伏侯龍恩、龍恩弟大將軍萬壽、大將軍劉勇、中外府司錄尹公正、袁傑、膳部下大夫李安等，於殿中殺之。

translations.literal: When Hu was killed, he then summoned the palace masters Zhangsun Lan and others and at once ordered the arrest of Hu's sons Pillar-of-State Tan Duke Hui, Grand General Ju Duke Zhi, Duke of Chongye Jing, Duke of Zhengping Qianjia, and Qianji, Qianwei, Qianzu, Qianwei, together with Pillar-of-State Houfu Hou Longen, Longen's younger brother Grand General Wanshou, Grand General Liu Yong, Palace and Exterior Bureau registrar Yin Gongzheng, Yuan Jie, Kitchen Service subordinate grand master Li An, and others, and killed them in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was killed, he summoned the palace masters Zhangsun Lan and others and at once ordered the arrest of Hu's sons Pillar-of-State Tan Duke Hui, Grand General Ju Duke Zhi, Duke of Chongye Jing, Duke of Zhengping Qianjia, and Qianji, Qianwei, Qianzu, and Qianwei, together with Pillar-of-State Houfu Hou Longen, Longen's younger brother Grand General Wanshou, Grand General Liu Yong, Palace and Exterior Bureau registrar Yin Gongzheng, Yuan Jie, Kitchen Service subordinate grand master Li An, and others, and killed them in the hall.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲曰：「安出自阜隸，所典庖廚而已，未足加戮。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi, said: "Li An came from the black-clad ranks; what he managed was only the kitchen—not enough to merit execution."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi, said: "Li An came from the black-clad ranks; what he managed was only the kitchen—not enough to merit execution — so the record states."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝不知耳，世宗之崩，安所為也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You do not know—Emperor Shizong's death was Li An's doing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You do not know—Emperor Shizong's death was Li An's doing — so the record states."

sentences.zh: 十九日，乃詔暴護等罪，大赦，改天和七年為建德元年。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day, an edict exposed the crimes of Hu and the others, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the seventh year of Tianhe was changed to the first year of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day, an edict exposed the crimes of Yuwen Hu and his faction, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and the seventh year of Tianhe was changed to the first year of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 護世子訓為蒲州刺史，其夜遣柱國越公盛乘傅鎮蒲州，征訓赴京師，至同州賜死。

translations.literal: Hu's heir Xun was governor of Pu Province; that night Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Yue, was sent by post relay to garrison Pu Province, to summon Xun to the capital; when he reached Tong Province he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's heir Xun was governor of Pu Province; that night Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Yue, was sent by post relay to garrison Pu Province and summon Xun to the capital; when he reached Tong Province he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 護長史叱羅協、司錄馮遷及所親任者皆除名。

translations.literal: Hu's chief administrator Chi Luoxie, registrar Feng Qian, and those he personally favored and entrusted were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's chief administrator Chi Luoxie, registrar Feng Qian, and those he personally favored and entrusted were all struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 護子昌城公深使突厥，遣開府宇文德齊璽書就殺之。
