translations.literal: Hu's son Yuwen Shen, Duke of Changcheng, was on mission to the Turks; an edict was sent with Palace Opener Yuwen De bearing the imperial seal to kill him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's son Yuwen Shen, Duke of Changcheng, was on mission to the Turks; Palace Opener Yuwen De was sent with an imperial-seal letter to kill him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔復護及諸子先封，諡護曰蕩，並改葬之。

translations.literal: Third year, an edict restored Hu and his sons' former enfeoffments, posthumously titled Hu Dang, and reburied them all.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, an edict restored Yuwen Hu and his sons' former enfeoffments, posthumously titled Hu Dang, and reburied them all.

sentences.zh: 叱羅協，代郡人，本名與武帝諱同，後改焉。

translations.literal: Chi Luoxie was a man of Dai commandery; his original given name was the same as Emperor Wu's taboo, and was later changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie was a man of Dai commandery; his original given name was the same as Emperor Yuwen Yong's taboo name, and was later changed.

sentences.zh: 少寒微，嘗為州小吏，以恭謹見知。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and humble; he once served as a minor clerk in the province and was known for respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was poor and humble; he once served as a minor clerk in the province and was known for respectful care — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 竇泰為御史中尉，以協為書侍御史。

translations.literal: When Dou Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Chi Luoxie investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Chi Luoxie investigating censor — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 泰向潼關，協為監軍。

translations.literal: When Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Xie was army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Chi Luoxie was army overseer.

sentences.zh: 泰死，協見獲。

translations.literal: When Dou Tai died, Chi Luoxie was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai died, Chi Luoxie was also captured — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 文帝授大丞相東合祭酒，累遷相府屬、從事中郎。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor appointed him eastern pavilion libationer of the grand chancellor's office, and he was repeatedly promoted to staff member of the chancellor's office and attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai appointed him eastern pavilion libationer of the grand chancellor's office, and he was repeatedly promoted to staff member of the chancellor's office and attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 協曆事二京，詳練故事，又深自克勵，文帝頗委任之。

translations.literal: Chi Luoxie served through both capitals and was thoroughly versed in precedent; moreover he deeply restrained himself, and Grand Progenitor greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie served through both capitals and was thoroughly versed in precedent; moreover he deeply restrained himself, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai greatly entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 然猶以家屬在東，疑其戀本。

translations.literal: Yet still, because his family remained in the east, he was suspected of longing for his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Yet still, because his family remained in the east, he was suspected of longing for his native place — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 及河橋戰敗，協隨軍還。

translations.literal: When the battle at He Bridge was lost, Chi Luoxie returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle at He Bridge was lost, Chi Luoxie returned with the army — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 文帝知協不貳，封冠軍縣男，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor knew Chi Luoxie was not double-minded and enfeoffed him as Baron of Champion county, advancing his rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai knew Chi Luoxie was not double-minded and enfeoffed him as Baron of Champion county, advancing his rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 後為大將軍尉遲迥長史，率兵伐蜀，行潼州事。

translations.literal: Later he served as chief administrator to Grand General Yuchi Jiong, led troops to attack Shu, and administered Tong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as chief administrator to Grand General Yuchi Jiong, led troops to attack Shu, and administered Tong Province affairs — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，文帝征協入朝，論蜀中事，乃賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Third year of Western Wei Emperor Gong, Grand Progenitor summoned Chi Luoxie to court to discuss affairs in Shu, then granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Western Wei Emperor Gong, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned Chi Luoxie to court to discuss affairs in Shu, then granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 晉公護既殺孫恆、李植等，欲委腹心于司會柳慶、司憲令狐整等，二人並辭，俱薦協。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu having killed Sun Heng, Li Zhi, and others, wished to entrust his inner core to Director of Retainers Liu Qing and Director of Censors Linghu Zheng and others; the two both declined and together recommended Chi Luoxie.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, having killed Sun Heng, Li Zhi, and others, wished to entrust his inner circle to Director of Retainers Liu Qing and Director of Censors Linghu Zheng and others; both declined and together recommended Chi Luoxie.

sentences.zh: 護遂征協入朝，引與同宿，深寄託之。

translations.literal: Hu then summoned Chi Luoxie to court, received him to lodge together, and deeply entrusted himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu then summoned Chi Luoxie to court, received him to lodge together, and deeply entrusted himself to him.

sentences.zh: 協誓以軀命自效。

translations.literal: Chi Luoxie vowed to give his life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie vowed to give his life in service — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 護大悅，以為得協之晚。

translations.literal: Hu was greatly pleased and thought he had gained Xie too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu was greatly pleased and thought he had gained Chi Luoxie too late.

sentences.zh: 稍遷護府長史，進爵為公，常在護側。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to chief administrator of Hu's office, advanced to duke, and constantly at Hu's side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to chief administrator of Yuwen Hu's office, advanced to duke, and constantly at Yuwen Hu's side.

sentences.zh: 明帝知其材識庸淺，每按抑之，數謂曰：「汝何知也！」

translations.literal: Emperor Ming knew his talent and knowledge were shallow and mediocre, and always cut him down, often telling him: "What do you know!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming knew his talent and knowledge were shallow and mediocre, and always cut him down, often telling him: "What do you know!."

sentences.zh: 猶以護所親任，每含容之。

translations.literal: Yet because Hu trusted and relied on him, each time they made allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Yuwen Hu trusted and relied on him, each time they made allowances.

sentences.zh: 及明帝崩，便授協司會中大夫、中外府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Chi Luoxie was promptly appointed Director of Audits grand master and chief secretary of the Palace and Exterior Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Chi Luoxie was promptly appointed Director of Audits grand master and chief secretary of the Palace and Exterior Bureau — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 協形貌瘦小，舉措偏急，既以得志，每自矜高；

translations.literal: Chi Luoxie was slight in build and small in stature; in manner he was narrow and hasty; once he had achieved his ambitions, he constantly vaunted himself;
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie was slight in build and small in stature; in manner he was narrow and hasty; once he had achieved his ambitions, he constantly vaunted himself;.

sentences.zh: 及其所言，多乖事衷，當時莫不笑之。

translations.literal: what he said often missed the point, and at the time everyone laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: What he said often missed the point, and at the time everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 護以其忠己，每提獎之。

translations.literal: Hu, because he was loyal to himself, constantly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, because he was loyal to him, constantly praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 協既受護重委，冀得婚連帝室，乃求復舊姓叱羅氏，許之。

translations.literal: Since Chi Luoxie had received Hu's heavy commission, he hoped to marry into the imperial house and therefore asked to restore his former surname, the Chi Luoxie clan; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chi Luoxie had received Yuwen Hu's heavy commission, he hoped to marry into the imperial house and therefore asked to restore his former surname, the Chi Luoxie clan; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 又進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was again advanced to pillar-of-state — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 護以協年老，許其致仕，而協貪榮，未肯告退。

translations.literal: Hu, considering Xie was old, permitted him to retire from office, but Xie, greedy for glory, was unwilling to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, considering Chi Luoxie was old, permitted him to retire from office, but Chi Luoxie, greedy for glory, was unwilling to resign.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，除名。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Chi Luoxie was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Chi Luoxie was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，以協宿齒，授儀同三司、賜爵南陽郡公。

translations.literal: Third year of Jiande, because Chi Luoxie was advanced in years, he was appointed grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and granted the title Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande, because Chi Luoxie was advanced in years, he was appointed grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and granted the title Duke of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，子金剛嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jingang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Jingang succeeded him — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 馮遷字羽化，弘農人。

translations.literal: Feng Qian, styled Yuhua, was a man of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian, styled Yuhua, was a man of Hongnong — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 少修謹，有幹能，為護府司錄。

translations.literal: From youth he was refined and cautious, possessed practical ability, and served as director of records of Hu's office.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was refined and cautious, possessed practical ability, and served as director of records of Yuwen Hu's office.

sentences.zh: 性質直，小心畏慎，兼明練時事，善於斷決，每校閱文簿，孜孜不倦，以此甚為護委任。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and cautious; he was also skilled and practiced in current affairs and good at deciding cases; each time he examined documents he was tireless—for this reason Hu greatly relied on and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and cautious; he was also skilled and practiced in current affairs and good at deciding cases; each time he examined documents he was tireless—for this reason Yuwen Hu greatly relied on and entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 後授陝州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed governor of Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed governor of Shaan Province — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 遷本寒微，不為時輩所重。

translations.literal: Feng Qian's origins were humble and the men of the age did not greatly esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian's origins were humble and the men of the age did not greatly esteem him — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 一旦刺舉本州，唯以廉恭接待鄉邑，人無怨者。

translations.literal: Once he held provincial oversight over his native commandery, he received his home district only with humility and respect, and no one bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held provincial oversight over his native commandery, he received his home district only with humility and respect, and no one bore resentment — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 復入為司錄，累遷小司空。

translations.literal: He again entered service as director of records and was repeatedly promoted to minor minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He again entered service as director of records and was repeatedly promoted to minor minister of works — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 自天和後，以年老，委任稍衰。

translations.literal: From Tianhe onward, because Feng Qian was old, his appointments gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianhe onward, because Feng Qian was old, his appointments gradually declined — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，猶除名。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, he too was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he too was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 子恕，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Shu held the post of grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu held the post of grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 杞簡公連，幼而謹厚，臨敵果毅。

translations.literal: Duke Lian of Qi, Lian, from youth was careful and honest, and in battle resolute and daring.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Lian of Qi, Yuwen Lian, was careful and honest from childhood and resolute in battle.

sentences.zh: 隨德皇帝遇定州軍于唐河，俱戰歿。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor De and encountered Ding Province troops at the Tang River; both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor De and encountered Ding Province troops at the Tang River; both died in battle — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒，封杞國公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, and grand minister of education; enfeoffed Duke of Qi; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, and grand minister of education; enfeoffed Duke of Qi; and given the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子元寶，為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbao was killed by Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanbao was killed by Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小司徒，襲封杞國公，諡曰烈，以章武公導子亮嗣。

translations.literal: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general and junior minister of education; inherited the dukedom of Qi, posthumous title Lie; Yuwen Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, became heir.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general and junior minister of education; inherited the dukedom of Qi with posthumous title Lie; Yuwen Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, became heir.

sentences.zh: 椿字乾壽，位上柱國、大司徒。

translations.literal: Chun, styled Qianshou, held the posts of supreme pillar-of-state and grand minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, styled Qianshou, held the posts of supreme pillar-of-state and grand minister of education — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 大定中，為隋文帝所害，並其五子。

translations.literal: In the Dading era he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his five sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era he was killed by Yuwen Tai, Emperor Wen of Zhou of Sui, together with his five sons.

sentences.zh: 莒莊公洛生，少任俠，好施愛士，北州賢俊皆與之遊，而才能多出其下。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang of Ju Yuwen Luosheng in youth was a bravo, generous and fond of nurturing talent; the worthy men of the northern provinces all associated with him, yet most fell short of his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang of Ju Yuwen Yuwen Luosheng in youth was a bravo, generous and fond of nurturing talent; the worthy men of the northern provinces all associated with him, yet most fell short of his ability.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮破鮮于修禮，以洛生為漁陽王，仍領德皇帝余眾，時人皆呼為洛生王。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he made Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and left him in command of Emperor De's remaining troops; contemporaries all called him the Luosheng Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he made Yuwen Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and left him in command of Emperor De's remaining troops; contemporaries all called him the Yuwen Luosheng Prince.

sentences.zh: 洛生善撫將士，是以克獲常冠諸軍。

translations.literal: Luosheng knew how to comfort soldiers, and therefore his captures usually topped those of every army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Luosheng knew how to comfort soldiers, and therefore his captures usually topped those of every army.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮定山東，時洛生在虜中，榮雅聞其名，心憚焉。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong settled Shandong, Luosheng was among the captives; Rong had long known his reputation and feared him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong settled Shandong, Yuwen Luosheng was among the captives; Rong had long known his reputation and feared him in his heart.

sentences.zh: 尋為榮所害。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Rong had him killed.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍，封莒國公，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general; enfeoffed Duke of Ju; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general; enfeoffed Duke of Ju; and given the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子菩薩，為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: His son Pusa was killed by Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pusa was killed by Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小宗伯，襲爵，諡曰穆，以晉公護子至嗣。

translations.literal: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general and junior clan elder; inherited the title, posthumous title Mu; Yuwen Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Hu, succeeded to the line.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding, he was posthumously made grand general and junior clan elder; inherited the title with posthumous title Mu; Yuwen Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 至字乾附，後坐父護誅，詔以衛王直子賓為穆公後。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Qianfu; later because of his father Hu's execution, an edict made Bin, son of Prince of Wei Zhi, heir to Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Qianfu; later because of his father Yuwen Hu's execution, an edict made Bin, son of Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi, heir to Duke Mu.

sentences.zh: 賓字乾瑞，尋坐直誅，而齊王憲子廣都郡公貢襲。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Qianrui; soon afterward he was executed for Prince Zhi's crime, and Gong, son of Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian, Guangdu commandery duke, succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Qianrui; soon afterward he was executed for Prince Yuwen Zhi's crime, and Gong, Guangdu commandery duke, son of Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 貢字乾貞，宣帝初，被誅，國除。

translations.literal: Gong, styled Qianzhen; at the opening of Emperor Xuan's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, styled Qianzhen; at the opening of Emperor Yuwen Yun's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 虞國公仲，德皇帝從父兄也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Yuwen Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 卒於代。

translations.literal: He died in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dai — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒，封虞國公。

translations.literal: At the opening of Baoding, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Minister of Education; enfeoffed Duke of Yuguo.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made grand tutor, pillar-of-state grand general, and grand minister of education, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuguo.

sentences.zh: 子興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing succeeded — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 興生，屬兵亂，與仲相失，年幼莫知其戚屬遠近，與文帝兄弟，初不相識。

translations.literal: Xing was born; it was a time of military turmoil. He was separated from Zhong, young and not knowing the nearness or distance of his kinship; with Emperor Wen's brothers he at first did not know one another.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was born amid the turmoil of war. Separated from Zhong while still young, he did not know how close or distant his kinship was, and he and Emperor Wen's brothers had at first not known one another.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，預在行間，被虜，隨例散配諸軍。

translations.literal: At the defeat at Shayuan he was among the ranks, taken captive; according to precedent he was dispersed and assigned to various armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the defeat at Shayuan he was caught in the ranks, taken captive, and by custom parceled out and assigned to various armies.

sentences.zh: 興性弘厚，有志度，雖流離世故，而風範可觀。

translations.literal: Xing's nature was broad and generous, with purpose and measure; though adrift through worldly vicissitudes, his bearing was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was broad and generous by nature, with breadth of purpose; though he had been adrift through the turns of fortune, his bearing was admirable.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，詔訪仲子孫，興始附屬籍。

translations.literal: In Baoding year 2 an edict sought Zhong's descendants; Xing was then attached to the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding an edict sought Zhong's descendants, and Xing was then entered on the clan register.

sentences.zh: 武帝以興帝戚近屬，尊禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Xing was a close imperial relative, honored and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, seeing that Xing was a close imperial kinsman, honored and treated him with great deference.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同三司、宗師，襲爵虞國公。

translations.literal: He held the offices of Opening-Office Equal-in-Three-Departments and Imperial Preceptor, and inherited the title Duke of Yuguo.
translations.idiomatic: He held opening-office equal-in-three-departments rank and served as imperial preceptor, and inherited the title Duke of Yuguo.

sentences.zh: 薨，武帝親臨慟焉。

translations.literal: He died; Emperor Wu came in person and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Wu came in person to mourn and grieve.

sentences.zh: 詔大司空、申國公李穆監護喪事，贈柱國大將軍，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: An edict put Li Mu, Duke of Shen and Grand Minister of Works, in charge of the funeral; posthumously granted Pillar-of-State Grand General; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li Mu, Duke of Shen and grand minister of works, to oversee the funeral; Xing was posthumously made pillar-of-state grand general, with posthumous name Jing (Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 子洛嗣，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Luo succeeded; he held the rank Equal-in-Three-Departments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo succeeded him and held the rank equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 隋初為介國公，為隋室賓云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui he was made Duke of Jie, declared a guest of the house of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui he was made Duke of Jie, declared to be a guest of the house of Sui.

sentences.zh: 廣川公測，字澄鏡，文帝之族子也。

translations.literal: Duke of Guangchuan Ce, styled Chengjing, was a clansman of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Guangchuan Yuwen Ce, styled Chengjing, was a clansman of Emperor Wen Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 高祖中山、曾祖豆頺、祖騏麟、父永，仕魏，位並顯達。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhongshan, great-great-grandfather Doutui, grandfather Qilin, and father Yong—all served Wei and rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears Zhongshan, Doutui, Qilin, and his father Yong had all served Northern Wei and risen to prominent rank.

sentences.zh: 測性沉密，少篤學詣，仕魏，位司徒右長史，尚宣武女陽平公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Ce's nature was grave and secretive; in youth he devoted himself to learning. He served Wei as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, married Princess Yangping, daughter of Emperor Xuanwu, and was appointed Commandant of Horse Guards Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce was grave and reserved by nature and devoted himself to learning from youth. He served Wei as right chief clerk of the minister of education, married Princess Yangping, daughter of Emperor Xuanwu, and was made commandant of horse guards consort.

sentences.zh: 及孝武疑齊神武，詔測詣文帝，密為之備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu suspected Gao Huan, he ordered Ce to visit Emperor Wen and make secret preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu suspected Gao Huan of disloyal intent, he ordered Yuwen Ce to visit Emperor Wen and make secret preparations on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 還，封廣川縣伯。

translations.literal: On his return he was enfeoffed Baron of Guangchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was enfeoffed as baron of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 尋從孝武西遷，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Emperor Xiaowu's westward move and was raised to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Emperor Xiaowu west and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 文帝為丞相，以測為右長史，委以軍國，又令測詳定宗室昭穆遠近，附於屬籍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became chancellor, he made Ce right chief clerk, entrusted him with military and state affairs, and also had Ce clarify the imperial clan by seniority and distance and enter them on the register.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen became chancellor, he made Yuwen Ce right chief clerk and entrusted him with military and state affairs; he also put Yuwen Ce in charge of sorting the imperial clan by seniority and distance and entering them on the register.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中、開府儀同三司，行汾州事。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of palace attendant, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and acting governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as palace attendant, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and acting governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 政在簡惠，頗得人和。

translations.literal: His government aimed at simplicity and kindness and won the people's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with simplicity and kindness and won the people to him.

sentences.zh: 地接東魏，數相抄竊，或有獲其為寇者，多縛送之。

translations.literal: The territory bordered Eastern Wei; cross-border raids were frequent. When raiders were captured, they were often bound and sent in.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Eastern Wei, where cross-border theft was frequent; captured raiders were often bound and sent in.

sentences.zh: 測皆命解縛，置之賓館，然後引與相見，如客禮焉。

translations.literal: Ce always ordered their bonds cut, lodged them in the guest house, then received them with the courtesy due to guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce always had their bonds cut, lodged them as guests, and only then received them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 仍宴設，放還其國，衛送出境。

translations.literal: He then set out a feast, sent them back to their state, and escorted them out of the border.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted them, sent them home, and had them escorted safely across the border.

sentences.zh: 自是東魏人大慚，乃不為寇，兩界遂通慶吊，時論方之羊叔子。

translations.literal: Thereafter the people of Eastern Wei were deeply ashamed and ceased raiding; the two borders then exchanged congratulations and condolences, and opinion at the time compared him to Yang Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Eastern Wei people were ashamed and stopped raiding; the two sides began to exchange congratulations and condolences, and contemporary opinion ranked him with Yang Hu.

sentences.zh: 或有告測懷貳，文帝怒曰：「測為我安邊，何為間骨肉！」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Ce harbored disloyal intent. Emperor Wen said in anger: "Ce secures my frontier for me—why would you sow discord among my flesh and blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yuwen Ce harbored disloyal intent. Emperor Wen raged: "Yuwen Ce holds my frontier—why would you sow discord among my kin!"

sentences.zh: 乃命斬之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the accuser executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had the accuser executed.

sentences.zh: 仍許測便宜從事。

translations.literal: He still allowed Ce full discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He still allowed Yuwen Ce full discretion in local affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉行綏州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting charge of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to acting governor of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 每歲河冰合後，突厥即來寇掠。

translations.literal: Each year after the Yellow River froze, the Turks would come raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Each year after the Yellow River froze, the Turks came raiding.

sentences.zh: 先是，常預遣居人入城堡以避之。

translations.literal: Previously, people were routinely sent into castles and forts to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuwen Ce arrived, people were routinely sent into walled towns to avoid the raids.

sentences.zh: 測至，皆令安堵。

translations.literal: When Ce arrived, he let everyone settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Ce arrived, he let everyone stay at home in peace.

sentences.zh: 乃於要路數百處並多積柴，仍遠斥候，知其動靜。

translations.literal: He then stacked firewood at hundreds of key points along the roads and posted scouts far out to learn enemy movements.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked firewood at hundreds of key points along the roads and posted scouts far out to watch enemy movements.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，突厥從連穀入寇，去界數十里，測命積柴處一時縱火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month that year the Turks invaded through Liangu; when they were several tens of li from the border, Ce ordered all the firewood piles set ablaze at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month that year the Turks invaded through Liangu and came within several tens of li of the border; Yuwen Ce ordered all the firewood piles set ablaze at once.

sentences.zh: 突厥謂大軍至，懼而遁走，委棄雜畜輜重不可勝數。

translations.literal: The Turks thought a great army had arrived, fled in fear, and abandoned livestock and baggage beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks thought a great army had arrived, fled in panic, and abandoned countless livestock and baggage.

sentences.zh: 自是不敢復至。

translations.literal: From then on they did not dare come again.
translations.idiomatic: After that they did not dare return.

sentences.zh: 測因請置戍以備之。

translations.literal: Ce then requested that garrison troops be posted as a defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce then asked that garrison troops be posted as a permanent defense.

sentences.zh: 後卒于太子少保，文帝親臨慟焉，仍令水池公監護喪事，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Later he died in the office of Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince; Emperor Wen came in person to grieve, put Duke of Chishui in charge of the funeral, and gave the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as junior preceptor to the crown prince; Emperor Wen mourned in person, put the Duke of Chishui in charge of the funeral, and gave him the posthumous name Jing (Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 測性仁恕，好施與。

translations.literal: Ce's nature was benevolent and forgiving; he loved to give.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce was benevolent and forgiving and generous by nature.

sentences.zh: 在洛陽之日，曾被竊盜，所失物即其妻陽平公主之衣服也。

translations.literal: While living in Luoyang he was once robbed; what was lost was clothing belonging to his wife Princess Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Luoyang he was once robbed of clothing belonging to his wife, Princess Yangping.

sentences.zh: 州縣禽盜，並物俱獲。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county caught the thief and recovered the goods together.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was caught and the stolen goods were recovered.

sentences.zh: 測恐此盜坐之以死，不認焉，遂遇赦免。

translations.literal: Ce feared this thief would be sentenced to death for it and would not identify the goods; he then met with an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce feared the thief would be sentenced to death if the goods were identified, so he would not claim them; the thief was spared when an amnesty came.

sentences.zh: 盜既感恩，請為測左右、及測從孝武西遷，事極狼狽，盜人亦從測入關，並無異志。

translations.literal: The thief, grateful, asked to serve at Ce's side; when Ce followed Emperor Xiaowu west in extreme disorder, the thief also followed Ce through the pass and showed no disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, the thief asked to serve as Yuwen Ce's attendant; when Yuwen Ce followed Emperor Xiaowu's westward flight in chaos, the man followed him through the pass and showed no disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 子該嗣，位除州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Gai succeeded; he held the post of governor of Chu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai succeeded him and served as governor of Chu Province.

sentences.zh: 測弟深。

translations.literal: Ce's younger brother was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce's younger brother was Yuwen Shen.

sentences.zh: 深字奴於，性鯁正，有器局。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Nuyu, was upright and principled by nature, with breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen, styled Nuyu, was upright and principled by nature, with breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，便累石為營，折草作旌旗，佈置行伍，皆有軍陣之勢。

translations.literal: At several years of age he would pile stones into camps, break grass to make banners, and draw up ranks—all with the look of battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: As a small child he stacked stones into camps, fashioned grass into banners, and drew up ranks with the look of real battle formations.

sentences.zh: 父永遇見之，喜曰：「汝自然知此，後必為名將。」

translations.literal: His father Yong saw it and said in delight: "You take to this by nature—you will surely be a famous general in the future."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong saw it and said in delight: "You take to this by nature—you will be a famous general someday."

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，事起倉卒，人多逃散。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, the affair arose in haste and many men scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, the crisis came suddenly and many men scattered.

sentences.zh: 深時為子都督，領宿衛兵，撫循所部，並得入關。

translations.literal: Shen was then a sub-commander leading palace guard troops; he comforted and guided his command and brought them all through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen was then a guard commander leading palace troops; he kept his command together and brought them all through the pass.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵長樂縣伯。

translations.literal: For this merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was enfeoffed as baron of Changle.

sentences.zh: 大統中，累轉尚書直事郎中。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he was repeatedly promoted to direct-affairs gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era he rose through repeated promotions to direct-affairs gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武屯蒲阪，分遣其將竇泰趨潼關，高敖曹圍洛州。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan encamped at Puban he sent his general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass while Gao Aocao besieged Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan encamped at Puban he sent his general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass while Gao Aocao besieged Luo Province — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 周文帝將襲泰，諸將咸難之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen planned to strike Dou Tai; the generals all found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen planned a surprise attack on Dou Tai, but the generals all opposed it.

sentences.zh: 帝隱其事，陽若未有謀，獨問策於深。

translations.literal: The emperor concealed his plan, outwardly as if he had no design, and consulted Shen alone for a strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hid his plan, feigning indecision, and consulted Yuwen Shen alone.

sentences.zh: 深曰：「竇氏，高歡驍將，歡每仗之禦侮。

translations.literal: Shen said: "The Dou clan—Gao Huan's fierce general; Huan always relies on him to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen said: "Dou Tai is Gao Huan's fiercest general; Huan always relies on him to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今大軍就蒲阪，則歡拒守，竇必援之，內外受敵，取敗道也。

translations.literal: If the main army now moves on Puban, Huan will stand on the defensive and Dou will certainly come to his aid—attacked within and without, this is the road to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If our main force moves on Puban, Gao Huan will stand on the defensive and Dou Tai will come to his aid; attacked from within and without, that is the road to defeat.

sentences.zh: 不如選輕銳潛出小關，竇性躁急，必來決戰，高歡持重，未即救之，則竇可禽也。

translations.literal: Better to choose elite light troops and slip out through Xiao Pass. Dou's nature is rash and urgent—he will surely come out to fight; Gao Huan is cautious and will not rescue him at once—then Dou can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take elite light troops and slip out through Xiao Pass. Dou Tai is hot-tempered and will come out to fight; Gao Huan is cautious and will not rescue him at once—then Dou Tai can be taken.

sentences.zh: 虜竇，歡勢自沮，回師禦之，可以制勝。」

translations.literal: Once Dou is captured, Huan's spirit will break of itself; turn back to meet him and you can win."
translations.idiomatic: Once Dou Tai is taken, Gao Huan's spirit will break; turn back and meet him and you can win."

sentences.zh: 文帝喜曰：「是吾心也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said gladly: "That is exactly my thought."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai, Emperor Wen of Zhou said gladly: "That is exactly my thought."

sentences.zh: 軍遂行，果獲泰，齊神武亦退。

translations.literal: The army marched; Dou Tai was indeed captured and Gao Huan also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched; Dou Tai was taken and Gao Huan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 深又說文帝進取弘農，復克之。

translations.literal: Shen also urged Emperor Wen to take Hongnong, and it was captured again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen also urged an advance on Hongnong, which was taken again.

sentences.zh: 文帝大悅，謂深曰：「君即吾家陳平也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased and told Shen: "You are our own Chen Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was delighted and told Yuwen Shen: "You are our own Chen Ping."

sentences.zh: 深少喪父，事兄甚謹。

translations.literal: Shen lost his father young and served his elder brother with scrupulous devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen lost his father as a boy and served his elder brother Yuwen Ce with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 性多奇譎，好讀兵書，既居近侍，每進籌策。

translations.literal: His nature was full of stratagems; he loved reading military books. Once he served close at hand, he often offered plans.
translations.idiomatic: Inventive and cunning by nature, he loved military treatises; once at the sovereign's side, he often offered strategic counsel.

sentences.zh: 及在選曹，頗有時譽。

translations.literal: When he was in the Selection Bureau he won considerable contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Selection Bureau he won considerable contemporary esteem.

sentences.zh: 性仁愛，從弟神舉、神慶幼孤，深撫訓之，義均同氣，世亦以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Kind by nature, he reared and taught his younger cousins Shenju and Shenqing, who were orphaned young, with the same affection as full brothers; the age also praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Kind by nature, he reared his younger cousins Yuwen Shenju and Yuwen Shenqing, orphaned as boys, with the affection of full brothers; his contemporaries praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 卒于位，諡曰成康。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous name Chengkang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his posthumous name was Chengkang.

sentences.zh: 子孝伯。

translations.literal: His son was Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yuwen Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 皇太子既無令德，孝伯言于帝曰：「皇太子德聲未聞，請妙選正人為其師友，調護聖質，不然，悔無所及。」

translations.literal: The crown prince already lacked worthy conduct. Xiaobo said to the emperor: "The crown prince's virtuous reputation has not been heard. Please choose excellent upright men as his teachers and friends to nurture his sacred character—otherwise regret will have no limit."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince already showed little worthy conduct. Yuwen Xiaobo said to the emperor: "We have not heard a virtuous reputation from the crown prince. Please choose worthy upright men as his teachers and friends to nurture his character—otherwise it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 帝斂容曰：「卿世載鯁正，竭誠所事，觀卿此言，有家風矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor composed his expression and said: "Your house has been upright for generations and you serve with full loyalty. Seeing these words of yours, there is the spirit of your family."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew grave and said: "Your house has been upright for generations and you serve with full loyalty. From what you say, I see the spirit of your family."

sentences.zh: 孝伯拜謝曰：「非言之難，受之難也，深願陛下思之。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo bowed in thanks and said: "It is not that speaking is hard, but that being heard is hard; I deeply wish Your Majesty would ponder this."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo bowed and replied: "The hard part is not speaking, but being heard. I earnestly beg Your Majesty to weigh this."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「正人豈復過君？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Where would an upright man surpass you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Where would I find an upright man better than you?"

sentences.zh: 於是以尉遲運為右宮正，孝伯仍為左宮正、宗師中大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuchi Yun was made right palace tutor and Xiaobo remained left palace tutor and middle grand master of the preceptorate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yuchi Yun was appointed right palace tutor and Xiaobo remained left palace tutor and middle grand master of the preceptorate.

sentences.zh: 累遷右宮伯。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to right palace tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right palace tutor.

sentences.zh: 嘗因侍坐，帝問：「我兒比進不？」

translations.literal: Once while attending in audience, the emperor asked: "Has my son been making progress lately?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while in attendance, the emperor asked: "Has my son been making progress lately?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「皇太子比懼天威，更無罪失。」

translations.literal: He answered: "The crown prince, lately fearing imperial majesty, has no more faults."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Lately the crown prince has been in awe of your majesty and has not repeated his faults."

sentences.zh: 及王軌因內宴捋帝須，言太子之不善。

translations.literal: When Wang Gui at an inner banquet seized the emperor's beard and spoke of the crown prince's faults,
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gui at a private banquet seized the emperor's beard and spoke of the crown prince's misconduct,

sentences.zh: 帝罷酒，責孝伯曰：「公常謂我雲太子無過，今軌有此言，公為誑矣。」

translations.literal: the emperor ended the drinking and reproached Xiaobo: "You always told me the crown prince had no faults; now Gui says this—you have deceived me."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ended the feast and reproached Xiaobo: "You always told me the crown prince had no faults; now Gui says this—you have misled me."

sentences.zh: 孝伯拜曰：「臣聞父子之際，人所難言，臣知陛下不能割情忍愛，遂爾結舌。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo bowed and said: "I have heard that between father and son there are things men find hardest to speak of; I knew Your Majesty could not bear to cut off affection and love, and so I held my tongue."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo bowed and said: "Between father and son there are things men find hardest to say. I knew Your Majesty could not bear to cut off affection, and so I kept silent."

sentences.zh: 帝知其意，默然久之，乃曰：「朕已委公，公其勉之。」

translations.literal: The emperor understood his meaning, was silent a long while, then said: "I have already entrusted matters to you—do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood, was silent a long while, then said: "I have already entrusted this to you—do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 及大軍東討，拜內史下大夫，令掌留台事。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east to campaign, he was made under director of the internal secretariat and ordered to hold the capital in the emperor's absence.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched east, he was made under director of the internal secretariat and ordered to hold the capital in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 軍還，帝曰：「居守之重，無忝戰功。」

translations.literal: Army returned; the emperor said: "The weight of holding the capital—no disgrace to battle merit."
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor said, "You held the capital well—your service matched the fighting merit."

sentences.zh: 於是加授大將軍，進爵廣陵郡公，並賜金帛女妓等。

translations.literal: He was then additionally granted the rank of grand general, raised to Duke of Guangling, and given gold, silk, and female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given the added rank of grand general, raised to duke of Guangling, and granted gold, silk, and female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 復為宗師。

translations.literal: He again served as imperial preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as imperial preceptor — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 每車駕巡幸，常令居守。

translations.literal: Each time the imperial carriage toured, he was always ordered to remain and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled, Xiaobo was left behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 後帝北討，至雲陽宮寢疾，驛召孝伯赴行在所，執其手曰：「吾自量必無濟理，以後事付君。」

translations.literal: Later when the emperor marched north and fell gravely ill at Yunyang Palace, he summoned Xiaobo by fast courier to the traveling palace and took his hand, saying: "I know I cannot recover—I entrust what follows to you."
translations.idiomatic: Later when the emperor marched north and fell gravely ill at Yunyang Palace, he summoned Xiaobo by fast courier to the traveling palace, took his hand, and said: "I know I cannot recover. I leave what follows to you."

sentences.zh: 是夜，授司衛上大夫，總宿衛兵馬，令馳驛入京鎮守。

translations.literal: That night he was made senior grand master of the palace guard with overall command of guard troops and ordered to ride posthaste to the capital to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he was made senior grand master of the palace guard with overall command of the guard troops and ordered to ride posthaste to the capital and hold it.

sentences.zh: 帝之西征也，在軍有過行，鄭譯時亦預焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned west, there were lapses in conduct in the army; Zheng Yi at the time also took part.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign the crown prince, later Emperor Xuan, had behaved badly in camp, and Zheng Yi had joined in.

sentences.zh: 軍還，孝伯及王軌盡以白武帝。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Xiaobo and Wang Gui reported everything to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Xiaobo and Wang Gui reported everything to Emperor Wu — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 武帝怒，撻帝數十，乃除譯名。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was furious, caned the crown prince dozens of times, and removed Zheng Yi from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was furious, caned the crown prince dozens of times, and removed Zheng Yi from office — so the record states.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝追憾被杖，乃問譯：「我腳上杖痕誰所為也？」

translations.literal: By then the emperor brooded over the beating and asked Zheng Yi: "Who left the cane marks on my legs?"
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor, brooding over the beating, asked Zheng Yi: "Who left the cane marks on my legs?"

sentences.zh: 譯曰：「事由宇文孝伯及王軌。」

translations.literal: Zheng Yi said: "The matter was Yuwen Xiaobo and Wang Gui."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi answered: "It was Yuwen Xiaobo and Wang Gui."

sentences.zh: 譯又說軌捋帝須事，帝乃誅軌。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi also spoke of Wang Gui seizing the emperor's beard; the emperor then had Wang Gui executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi also brought up Wang Gui's pulling the emperor's beard; the emperor then had Wang Gui executed.

sentences.zh: 尉遲運懼，私謂孝伯曰：「吾徒必不免禍，奈何？」

translations.literal: Yuchi Yun was afraid and said privately to Xiaobo: "Our sort will surely not escape disaster—what can we do?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yun was frightened and said privately to Xiaobo: "Our sort will surely not escape harm—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「有老母，地下有武帝，為臣為子，知欲何之！

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I have an old mother above and Emperor Wu below; as minister and as son, where would I go!
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo replied: "I have an old mother above and Emperor Wu below. As minister and as son, where would I go?

sentences.zh: 且委質事人，本徇名義，諫而不入，將焉逃死？

translations.literal: Besides, once you pledge yourself to serve others, you live for duty and reputation; if remonstrance is not accepted, how can you flee death?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, once you have pledged yourself to serve, you live and die for duty. If remonstrance is not heeded, how can you flee death?

sentences.zh: 足下若為身計，宜且遠之。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, take thought for yourself, you should for the time draw away."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to save yourself, you had better keep your distance for now."

sentences.zh: 於是各行其志。

translations.literal: Thereupon each followed his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: After that each did as he thought best.

sentences.zh: 運尋出為秦州總管。

translations.literal: Yun soon went out as Area Commander of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yun was soon sent out as area commander of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 帝荒淫日甚，誅戮無度。

translations.literal: The emperor grew daily more dissolute; executions were without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew more dissolute by the day and killed without restraint.

sentences.zh: 孝伯頻諫不從，由是益疏。

translations.literal: Xiaobo remonstrated frequently but was not heeded; for this he was further estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xiaobo remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen, and Xiaobo was pushed farther away.

sentences.zh: 後稽胡反，令孝伯為行軍總管，從越王盛討平之。

translations.literal: Later when the Ji Hu rebelled, he made Xiaobo campaign marshal and followed Prince of Yue Sheng to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji Hu rebelled later, Xiaobo was made campaign marshal and marched with Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng to put them down.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，帝將殺之，乃托以齊王事誚之曰：「公知齊王謀反，何以不言？」

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor was about to kill him; he used the Qi Wang affair as pretext, reproached him: "You knew Qi Wang plotted rebellion—why did you not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the emperor meant to kill him. Using the Prince of Qi as a pretext, he rebuked Xiaobo: "You knew the Prince of Qi was plotting rebellion—why did you say nothing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣知齊王忠於社稷，為群小媒蘖，加之以罪。

translations.literal: Xiaobo replied: "I knew Prince of Qi was loyal to the altars of state; petty men slandered and harmed him, adding crime to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo replied, "I knew the Prince of Qi was loyal to the state. Petty men slandered him and piled false charges upon him.

sentences.zh: 臣以言必不用，所以不言。

translations.literal: I reckoned speech would surely not be heeded, and so did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: I knew anything I said would be ignored, so I kept silent.

sentences.zh: 且先帝屬微臣輔陛下，今諫而不從，實負顧托。

translations.literal: Moreover the late emperor entrusted charge to this humble minister, only ordering me to assist and guide Your Majesty; now remonstrance is not heeded—I truly fail the entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor entrusted me only to guide Your Majesty. Now that my remonstrance goes unheeded, I have failed that charge.

sentences.zh: 以此為罪，是所甘心。」

translations.literal: To take this as crime—I gladly accept it."
translations.idiomatic: If that is my crime, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 帝慚，俯首不語。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly ashamed, bowed his head and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply ashamed and looked down without a word.

sentences.zh: 令賜死于家，時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was ordered granted death at home; he was thirty-six at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take death at home. He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝踐極，以孝伯、王軌忠而獲罪，並令收葬，復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, because Xiaobo and Wang Gui were faithful yet suffered punishment, together ordered them collected and buried, restoring their offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he had Xiaobo and Wang Gui reburied with honor and their offices and ranks restored, because both had been loyal men punished unjustly.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂高穎曰：「宇文孝伯實有周良臣，若此人在朝，我輩無措手處。」

translations.literal: He also once told Gao Jiong: "Yuwen Xiaobo was truly a good minister of Zhou; if this man had been in court, we would have had no room to act."
translations.idiomatic: He also once told Gao Jiong, "Yuwen Xiaobo was a true good minister of Zhou. If he had still been at court, we would have had no opening."

sentences.zh: 子歆嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin inherited his place.

sentences.zh: 東平公神舉，文帝之族子也。

translations.literal: Duke of Dongping Shenju was a clansman of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dongping Yuwen Shenju was a clansman of Yuwen Tai, Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖普陵、曾祖求男，仕魏位並顯達。

translations.literal: Great-great-grandfather Pul-ing, great-grandfather Qiuman — served Wei; offices both illustrious and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Pul-ing and great-grandfather Qiuman served Wei and both rose to prominent rank.

sentences.zh: 祖金殿，魏兗州刺史安喜縣侯。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jindian was Wei Inspector of Yan Province and Marquis of Anxi county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jindian was inspector of Yan Province under Wei and marquis of Anxi county.

sentences.zh: 父顯和，少而襲爵，性矜嚴，頗涉經史，膂力絕人，彎弓數百斤，能左右馳射。

translations.literal: Father Xianhe — from youth inherited enfeoffment; nature stern and strict; considerably crossed classics and histories; physical strength surpassed men; bent bow several hundred jin; able left and right gallop shoot.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianhe succeeded to the title while still young. Stern by nature and well read in the classics and histories, he had strength beyond ordinary men, could draw a bow of several hundred jin, and shoot with equal skill from either hand while riding.

sentences.zh: 孝武之在蕃，顯和早蒙眷遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was at fief, Xianhe early received favor and encounter.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu was still a frontier prince, Xianhe won his early favor.

sentences.zh: 時屬多難，嘗問計於顯和。

translations.literal: Time belonged to many difficulties; once asked plan from Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled times the emperor once asked Xianhe for counsel.

sentences.zh: 顯和具陳宜杜門晦跡，相時而動，帝深納焉。

translations.literal: Xianhe fully stated ought close doors and hide traces, watch time then move; the emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe urged him plainly to withdraw from sight, bide his time, and act when the moment came, and the emperor took this advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 及即位，拜閣內都督，封城陽縣公，以恩舊遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, appointed Inner Guard area commander, enfeoffed Duke of Chengyang county; because of old kindness treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne he made Xianhe inner guard area commander and enfeoffed him as duke of Chengyang, treating him with great favor from their old bond.

sentences.zh: 顯和所居隘陋，乃撤殿省賜為寢室，其見重如此。

translations.literal: Xianhe's dwelling was narrow and crude; thereupon palace offices were demolished and granted as bedchamber—thus seen and valued.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianhe's house proved cramped, the emperor tore down part of the palace offices and gave him the space for his quarters—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武專政，帝每不自安，問顯和曰：「天下洶洶，將如之何？」

translations.literal: When Gao Huan monopolized government, the emperor each time was not at ease; he asked Xianhe: "Under heaven turbulent and surging — what to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Huan dominated the government the emperor grew uneasy and asked Xianhe, "The realm is in turmoil — what shall I do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「莫若擇善而從。」

translations.literal: Replied: "None like choose good then follow."
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe answered, "The best course is to choose what is right and follow it."

sentences.zh: 因誦詩云：「彼美人兮，西方之人兮。」

translations.literal: Thereupon recited poem says: "That beautiful person — western region's person."
translations.idiomatic: and quoted the ode: "That fair one — a man of the west."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是吾心也。」

translations.literal: Emperor said: "This is my heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is my own thought."

sentences.zh: 遂定入關策。

translations.literal: Thereupon settled enter-Pass strategy.
translations.idiomatic: and so the plan to enter Guanzhong was decided.

sentences.zh: 以其母老，令預為計。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he ordered beforehand make plan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xianhe's mother was elderly, the emperor told him to make arrangements in advance.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今日之事，忠孝不並。

translations.literal: Replied: "Today's affair — loyalty and filial piety cannot together stand.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In the present crisis loyalty and filial duty cannot both be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 然臣不密則失身，安敢預為私計。」

translations.literal: Yet subject not secret then loses body; how dare beforehand make private plan."
translations.idiomatic: And if a minister is not discreet he risks his life — how could I make private plans beforehand?"

sentences.zh: 帝愴然改容曰：「卿，我之王陵也。」

translations.literal: The emperor grieved, changed countenance: "Lord — you are my Wang Ling."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed with sorrow as he said, "You are my Wang Ling."

sentences.zh: 遷硃衣直合、合內大都督，改封長廣縣公。

translations.literal: Transferred Crimson-Robe Direct Guard, Inside-Guard Great Area Commander; changed enfeoffment to Duke of Changguang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made crimson-robe direct guard and great area commander of the inner guard, and his title was changed to duke of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 從孝武入關。

translations.literal: He followed Xiaowu in entering the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 至溱水，周文帝素聞其善射而未之見，俄而水傍有一小鳥，顯和射中之。

translations.literal: Reaching the Qin River, Zhou Emperor Wen had long heard of his skill at archery but had not yet seen it; presently by the water there was a small bird, and Xianhe shot and hit it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qin River, Yuwen Tai had long heard of his archery but had not yet seen it. Soon a small bird appeared by the water, and Xianhe shot it down.

sentences.zh: 文帝笑曰：「我知卿工矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen laughed and said: "I know you are skilled."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai laughed and said, "I see you are a master."

sentences.zh: 進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal-in-Three-Departments, Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，追贈驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, posthumously granted Pillar-of-State Grand General and Opening-Office Equal-in-Three-Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande he was posthumously honored as grand general of the pillar of state and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 神舉見待于武帝，處心腹之任，王軌、宇文孝伯等屢言皇太子之短，神舉亦頗預焉。

translations.literal: Shenju was seen and treated at Emperor Wu, placed in trusted inner charge; Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo and others repeatedly spoke crown prince's faults — Shenju also participated.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju enjoyed Emperor Wu's trust and stood among his closest advisers; Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others often criticized the crown prince, and Shenju took part as well.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即位，荒淫無度，神舉懼及禍，懷不自安。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, dissolute beyond measure, Shenju feared disaster and was uneasy at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xuan took the throne and gave himself over to boundless excess, Shenju feared he would be caught up in ruin and could not feel secure.

sentences.zh: 初定范陽之後，威聲甚振，帝亦忌其名望，兼以宿憾，遂使人齎[CＧ]酒賜之，薨于馬邑，時年四十八。

translations.literal: After first pacifying Fanyang, his renown greatly shook; the emperor also envied his fame, together with old resentment, and sent someone bearing poisoned wine to grant him; he died at Mayi; he was forty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: After he first pacified Fanyang his reputation soared. The emperor resented his standing as well as an old grudge and sent an envoy with poisoned wine; Shenju died at Mayi at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 神舉美風儀，善辭令，博涉經史，性愛篇章，尤工奇射。

translations.literal: Shenju had a grand bearing, was skilled in speech, broadly versed in classics and histories, loved literary composition by nature, and was especially adept at strange archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju was imposing in presence, eloquent, widely read in the classics and histories, fond of writing by temperament, and especially masterful at remarkable mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 臨戎對寇，勇而有謀，蒞職當官，每著聲績。

translations.literal: Facing battle and confronting the foe, brave and resourceful; holding office and serving in post, he always achieved renown and merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the field against the enemy he was bold and shrewd, and in every post he held he won a name for solid achievement.

sentences.zh: 兼好施愛士，以雄豪自居，故得任兼文武，聲彰外內。

translations.literal: He also loved to bestow favors and cherish scholars, holding himself as a bold hero; thus he held posts combining civil and military roles, and his fame resounded within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous to men of talent and carried himself like a great champion, and so he served in both civil and military capacities until his reputation rang at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 百僚無不仰其風則，先輩舊齒至於今稱之。

translations.literal: None among the hundred officials failed to look up to him as a model; elders of former days even to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Every official looked up to him as a standard, and older contemporaries still speak of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 子同嗣，位至儀同大將軍，神舉弟慶。

translations.literal: His son Tong succeeded, reaching the rank of Equal-in-Protocol Grand General; Shenju's younger brother Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong inherited his place and rose to equal-in-protocol grand general. Shenju's younger brother was Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶字神慶，沈深有器局，少以敏見知。

translations.literal: Qing, styled Shenqing, was deep and reserved with breadth of capacity; from youth known for quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Qing, courtesy name Shenqing, was grave and far-seeing in temperament and was noted from youth for his keen mind.

sentences.zh: 初受業東觀，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: At first he received instruction at the Eastern Observatory and considerably crossed classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied at the Eastern Observatory and gained a solid grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 既而謂人曰：「書足記姓名而已，安能久事筆硯為腐儒業乎？」

translations.literal: Presently he told others: "Books suffice to record one's name—how can one long serve brush and ink and make a pedant's trade?
translations.idiomatic: He then said to others, "Books are enough to record one's name. How could one spend one's life at desk and ink and become a bookish pedant?

sentences.zh: 時文州賊亂，慶應募從征，以功授都督。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Province had bandit turmoil; Qing answered the call and followed the campaign; for merit granted area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Wen Province, Qing volunteered for the campaign and was made area commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 衛王直鎮山南，引為左右。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Zhi garrisoned south of the mountains and brought him in as a close attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi held the south of the mountains, he took Qing into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 慶善射，有膽氣，好格猛獸，直甚壯之。

translations.literal: Qing was skilled at archery, had daring spirit, loved grappling with fierce beasts; Zhi greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was an archer of courage who delighted in wrestling fierce beasts, and Zhi thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal-in-Three-Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 及誅宇文護，慶有謀焉。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Qing had a hand in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was put to death, Qing had taken part in the planning.

sentences.zh: 時授驃騎大將軍，加開府。

translations.literal: At the time granted Pillar-of-State Grand General and added Opening-Office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time he was made grand general of the pillar of state with the added rank of opening-office.

sentences.zh: 從武帝攻河陰，先登攀堞，與賊短兵接，中石乃墜，絕而後蘇。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in attacking Heyin, he was first to climb the ramparts; short weapons met the foe; struck by a stone he fell, lost consciousness, then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with Emperor Wu against Heyin, he was first up the wall. In close fighting he was struck by a stone, fell senseless, and then came to.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「卿勇可以賈人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him: "Your bravery could buy a city."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "Your courage could ransom a city."

sentences.zh: 復從武帝拔晉州，齊兵大至，慶與齊王憲輕騎覘之，卒與賊相遇，為賊所窘。

translations.literal: Again following Emperor Wu in taking Jinyang, Qi troops came in great force; Qing with Prince of Qi Xian rode light cavalry to reconnoiter; finally met the foe and was pressed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jinyang. When Qi forces arrived in strength, Qing and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian rode out with a light escort to scout and suddenly ran into the enemy and were hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 憲挺身而遁。

translations.literal: Xian threw himself forward and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xian broke free and escaped.

sentences.zh: 慶退據汾橋，眾賊爭進，慶射之，所中人馬必倒，賊乃稍卻。

translations.literal: Qing withdrew and held Fen Bridge; the mass of foes pressed forward; Qing shot them—those struck, man or horse, invariably fell; the foe then slightly retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Qing fell back to hold Fen Bridge. As the enemy surged forward he shot; every bolt felled man or horse, and the foe drew back a little.

sentences.zh: 及拔高壁，克并州，下信都，禽高湝，功並居最。

translations.literal: When Gaobi was taken, Bing Province captured, Xindu reduced, Gao Hui captured—the achievements all ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaobi was taken, Bingzhou conquered, Xindu subdued, and Gao Hui captured, his merit ranked first among all.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，封汝南郡公。

translations.literal: Advanced to Grand General, enfeoffed Duke of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general and enfeoffed as duke of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍總管擊延安反胡，平之。

translations.literal: Soon as campaign marshal he struck the rebellious Hu of Yan'an and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as campaign marshal, he attacked the rebellious Hu in Yan'an and put them down.

sentences.zh: 曆延、甯二州總管。

translations.literal: He successively served as area commander of Yan and Ning provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as area commander of Yan and Ning provinces.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，以行軍總管征江表，次白帝，以勞進上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, as campaign marshal he campaigned on the Jiang region, halted at Baidi, and for labor was advanced to Upper Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian was chief minister, Qing marched south as campaign marshal against the Jiang region, halted at Baidi, and was advanced to upper grand general for his exertions.

sentences.zh: 帝與慶有舊，甚見親待，令督丞相軍事，委以心腹。

translations.literal: The emperor and Qing had an old bond; he was greatly treated with intimacy; ordered to supervise the chief minister's military affairs and entrusted as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian and Qing were old associates, and Qing was treated with exceptional intimacy. He was ordered to oversee the chief minister's military affairs and entrusted as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 尋加柱國。

translations.literal: Soon added as Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the rank of pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜左武衛將軍，進上柱國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, appointed General of the Left Martial Guard; advanced to Upper Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang era he was made general of the left martial guard and advanced to upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 數年，除涼州總管。

translations.literal: Several years later, appointed area commander of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed area commander of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 歲余征還，不任以職。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year recalled from campaign; not entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he was recalled and given no further duties.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝龍潛時，嘗與慶言，謂曰：「天元質無積德，其相貌壽亦不長，加以法令繁苛，耽恣聲色，以吾觀之，殆將不久。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Wen was still in the wings, he once spoke with Qing, saying: "The Tianyuan Emperor's nature lacks accumulated virtue; his countenance and lifespan are also not long; moreover laws and orders are severe and intricate, indulging in sound and color—by my view, he will probably not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yang Jian was still biding his time, he once spoke with Qing and said, "Emperor Xuan's nature has no store of virtue; by his looks his life will not be long. With harsh laws and indulgence in pleasure, in my view he will not endure.

sentences.zh: 又諸侯微弱，各令就國，曾無深根固本之計，羽翮既翦，何及遠？

translations.literal: Moreover the feudal lords are weak; each is ordered to his state; never was there a plan to root deeply and secure the foundation; once the wings are clipped, what reaches far?
translations.idiomatic: The princes are weak, each sent to his own domain, with no plan to plant deep roots. Once their wings are clipped, how far can they go?

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥貴戚，早著聲望，國家有釁，必為亂階。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jiong is an honored kinsman, early renowned in reputation; if the state has a crack, he will surely be a source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong is a noble kinsman of long-standing fame; if the realm shows a breach, he is sure to become a source of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 然智量庸淺，子弟輕佻，貪而少惠，終致亡滅。

translations.literal: Yet his wisdom and measure are shallow and mediocre; sons and younger brothers are frivolous; greedy and little given to kindness—ultimately leading to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his mind is shallow, his sons and brothers reckless, greedy and sparing of grace, and he will end in destruction.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難反覆之虜，亦非池內之物，變在俄頃。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan is a shifting barbarian, also not a creature within the pool; change comes in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan is a fickle foe, not one to be kept in the pond; his turn will come in an instant.

sentences.zh: 但輕薄無謀，未能為害，不過自竄江南耳。

translations.literal: But light and thin without strategy, unable to become harm—no more than fleeing south of the Yangtze himself.
translations.idiomatic: But he is shallow and unresourceful and cannot do real harm—he will only flee south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 庸蜀險隘，易生艱阻，王謙愚蠢，素無籌略，但恐為人所誤，不足為虞。」

translations.literal: Yong and Shu are perilous and narrow, easily producing hardship and obstruction; Wang Qian is stupid, by nature without strategy—only feared to be misled by others, not enough to be a worry."
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Shu are rugged and easily breed trouble. Wang Qian is dull and has no stratagem; he may be led astray by others, but is hardly worth fearing."

sentences.zh: 未幾，上言皆驗。

translations.literal: Before long, the words above all proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, every prediction proved true.

sentences.zh: 及此，慶恐上遺忘，不復收用，欲見舊蒙恩顧，具錄前言，為表奏之。

translations.literal: By this time Qing feared the emperor had forgotten and would not again employ him; wishing to show he still enjoyed old favor, he fully recorded the former words and submitted them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qing feared the emperor had forgotten him and would not employ him again. Hoping to remind Yang Jian of past kindness, he set down his earlier words in full and submitted them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 上省表大悅，下詔曰：「朕言之驗，自是偶然；

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased; issued an edict: "That my words proved true was itself accidental;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with great pleasure and issued an edict: "That my words came true was mere chance;

sentences.zh: 公乃不忘，彌表誠節。

translations.literal: yet you did not forget—this all the more shows sincerity and constancy.
translations.idiomatic: yet you have not forgotten—this shows your loyalty all the more.

sentences.zh: 深感至意，嘉尚無已。」

translations.literal: I deeply feel your utmost intent; praise and esteem without end."
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply moved by your devotion and hold you in unceasing regard."

sentences.zh: 自是上每加優禮。

translations.literal: From this the emperor always added preferential treatment.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor treated him with added favor.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away at his residence.

sentences.zh: 子靜亂，尚隋文女廣平公主，位儀同、安德縣公、熊州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jingluan married Emperor Wen's daughter Princess Guangping; rank Equal-in-Protocol, Duke of Ande county, Inspector of Xiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingluan married Emperor Wen's daughter Princess Guangping and held the ranks of equal-in-protocol, duke of Ande county, and inspector of Xiong Province.

sentences.zh: 先慶卒。

translations.literal: He died before Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his father Qing.

sentences.zh: 靜亂子協，位右翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: Jingluan's son Xie, rank Right Assistant Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Jingluan's son Xie served as right assistant guard general.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，遇害。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Yuwen Huaji, he met with disaster and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the uprising of Yuwen Huaji he was killed.

sentences.zh: 協弟晶，字婆羅門，大業中養于宮內，後為千牛左右。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Jing, styled Boluomen, in the Daye era was raised in the palace; later became Thousand-Bull Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Jing, courtesy name Boluomen, was reared in the palace during the Daye era and later became a thousand-bull left guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝甚親昵之，每有遊宴，必侍從。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was very intimate with him; whenever there were excursions and banquets, he must attend.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang treated him with great intimacy and always had him attend banquets and outings.

sentences.zh: 至於出入臥內，伺察六宮，往來不限門禁。

translations.literal: As for entering and leaving the inner quarters, observing the six palaces, coming and going without limit of gate or prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He went in and out of the inner apartments, watched over the six palaces, and passed the gates without restriction.

sentences.zh: 時人號為宇文三郎。

translations.literal: People of the time called him the Third Son Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called him the Third Son Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 與宮人淫亂，至於妃嬪公主亦有醜聲。

translations.literal: He fornicated with palace women; even consorts and princesses had scandalous reports.
translations.idiomatic: He debauched palace women, and even imperial consorts and princesses were rumored to be involved.

sentences.zh: 蕭後言於帝，晶聞，懼不敢見。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao spoke to the emperor; when Jing heard, he feared and dared not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiao reported this to the emperor, Jing heard of it and was afraid to show himself.

sentences.zh: 協因奏晶壯，不可久在宮掖。

translations.literal: Xie thereupon memorialized that Jing was strong and could not long remain in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xie then memorialized that Jing was grown and should not remain long in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝不之罪，召入，待之如初。

translations.literal: The emperor did not blame him; summoned him in and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him, summoned him back, and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 化及殺逆際，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: At the moment of Huaji's regicide, he was harmed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji carried out his coup, Jing was killed by the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古受命之君及守文之王，非獨異姓之輔，亦有骨肉之助焉。

translations.literal: The historian writes: From antiquity, rulers who received the mandate and sovereigns who preserved the patrimony have relied not only on ministers of other surnames but also on assistance from flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From antiquity, founding rulers and heirs who kept the patrimony have relied not only on ministers outside the clan but also on help from royal kin.

sentences.zh: 其茂親則有魯衛、梁楚，其疏屬則有凡蔣、荊燕，咸能飛聲騰實，不滅於百代之後。

translations.literal: Among close kin were Lu, Wei, Liang, and Chu; among more distant kin Fan, Jiang, Jing, and Yan—all could raise their fame and prove their merit and did not perish after a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Close royal houses such as Lu, Wei, Liang, and Chu, and more distant ones such as Fan, Jiang, Jing, and Yan, all won renown and proved their merit and were not forgotten after a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 至若豳孝公之勳烈，加之以善政，蔡文公之純孝，飾之以儉約，峨峨焉足以轔轢於前載矣。

translations.literal: As for Duke Xiao of Bin's feats crowned by good government, and Duke Wen of Cai's pure filial piety graced by thrift—they tower, enough to eclipse the worthies of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Duke Xiao of Bin's feats of arms crowned by good government, and Duke Wen of Cai's pure filial devotion graced by thrift: towering figures, enough to eclipse the worthies of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 有周受命之始，宇文護實預艱難。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Zhou received the mandate, Yuwen Hu truly shared in the hardships.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning when Zhou received the mandate, Yuwen Yuwen Hu truly shared in the hardships.

sentences.zh: 及文後崩殂，諸子沖幼，群公懷等夷之士，天下有去就之心，卒能變魏為周，捍危獲義者，護之力也。

translations.literal: When Empress Wen died, the sons were young; the great lords harbored ambitions of equal standing and the realm had minds inclined to depart; that he could ultimately transform Wei into Zhou and bring order out of peril was Yuwen Hu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wen died, the sons were still young, the great lords harbored ambitions of equal standing, and the realm was ready to turn away; that he ultimately could transform Wei into Zhou and bring order out of peril was Yuwen Hu's strength.

sentences.zh: 向使加之以禮讓，經之以忠貞，桐宮有悔過之期，未央終天年之數，同前史所載，焉足道哉？

translations.literal: If only he had added humility and deference and continued in loyalty and constancy—if the Palace of the Tung tree had had a term for repentance and Weiyang Palace a full span of years—then as the earlier histories record, how would that be worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: If only he had added humility and deference and continued in loyalty and constancy—if the Palace of the Tung tree had had a term for repentance and Weiyang Palace a full span of years—then what the earlier histories record would scarcely be worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 然護寡於學術，昵近群小，威福在已，征伐自出，有人臣無君之心，為人主不堪之事，終於妻子為戮，身首橫分，蓋其宜也。

translations.literal: Yet Hu was poor in learning, drew close to petty men, kept favor and punishment in his own hands, and launched campaigns on his own authority; he had the heart of a minister without a lord and did what a sovereign cannot bear—in the end his wife and children were slaughtered and his body cut apart at the neck, which was only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuwen Hu was poor in learning, drew close to petty men, kept favor and punishment in his own hands, and launched campaigns on his own authority; he had the heart of a minister without a lord and did what a sovereign cannot bear. In the end his wife and children were slaughtered and his body was cut apart at the neck—is this not fitting?

sentences.zh: 當隋氏之起，假天威而服海內，胄以葭莩之親，據一州而協義舉，可謂忠而能勇。

translations.literal: When the house of Sui rose, borrowing Heaven's might to subdue the realm, Zhou, by the closest kinship, held one province and joined the righteous rising—this may be called loyal and brave.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Sui rose and, bearing Heaven's might, subdued the realm, Yuwen Zhou, by the closest kinship, held one province and joined the righteous rising—this may be called loyal and brave at once.

sentences.zh: 功業不遂，悲夫！

translations.literal: His enterprise went unfulfilled—alas!
translations.idiomatic: His enterprise went unfulfilled—alas!.

sentences.zh: 亮實庸才，圖非常於巨逆，古人稱不度德、不量力者，其斯之謂歟。

translations.literal: Liang was truly a mediocrity who plotted extraordinary action amid great treason; the ancients spoke of men who do not measure their virtue or their strength—is this not exactly what they meant?
translations.idiomatic: Liang was truly a mediocrity who plotted extraordinary action amid great treason. The ancients spoke of men who do not measure their virtue or their strength—is this not exactly what they meant?

sentences.zh: 宇文測兄弟驅馳于經綸之日，孝伯、神舉盡言于父子之間，觀其智勇忠概，並可追從于古人矣。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ce and his brothers rushed about in the days of statecraft; Xiaobo and Shenju spoke fully between father and son—viewing their wisdom, courage, loyalty, and spirit, all may be followed back to the men of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce and his brothers served in the days of founding the state; Yuwen Xiaobo and Yuwen Shenju spoke plainly between father and son. Judging their wisdom, courage, loyalty, and spirit, each could stand comparison with the worthies of antiquity.
